proposals.title: Data-declared tick schedule and hook chains that encode the full legacy order, test-enforced against step.ts and gameplay.ts
proposals.problem: The legacy order is not one list. It is 18 fixed phases in step.ts:242-296 plus three registration lists (afterWeapons 3, beforeDamage 3, systems 23), 7 move modifiers (their multiplication order matters under C-NUM, step.ts:269-272), 6 mod sources, 12 action handlers and 89 chainHook links over 27 hooks. All of these are ordered implicitly by the MODULES install order in gameplay.ts:35-83 and by push order inside each install(). The Rust port records this as 6 free-text bracket comments in sim.rs:736-768. The one ported system, flush_bounty_announcements (sim.rs:767), is legacy systems slot #5 (feed.flushAnnouncements). Four systems must run before it (factions.afterDamage, factions.healOverTime, mobs.resetDummies, buffs.expireBoosts), but the code says nothing about that, so P-FACTION-1 can put its afterDamage after it and still compile and pass today's fixtures. No test checks the order (C-TICK lists only 'parity suite'). That makes C-TICK depend on reviewers reading comments.
proposals.change:
New crates/rh-sim/src/schedule.rs holds the schedule as data:
```rust

pub struct Slot { pub legacy: &'static str, pub run: Run }
pub const ACTIVE: &[Slot] = &[
  slot("arena.markTickStart", ported(arena::mark_tick_start)),
  slot("step.applyInputs", ported(inputs::apply_all)),
  slot("abilities.updateAbilities", pending("P-ABIL-1")),
  slot("targeting.updateTargets", pending("P-COMBAT-3")),
  slot("weapons.updateWeapons", ported(weapons::update)),
  slot("factions.afterWeapons", pending("P-FACTION-1")), /* bruiserPassives.update, plagueZombies */
  slot("step.walkFighter", ported(movement::walk_all)), slot("movement.recordHistory", ported(movement::record_all)),
  slot("projectiles.sweepProjectiles", pending("P-COMBAT-2")), slot("projectiles.spawnProjectiles", pending("P-COMBAT-2")),
  slot("melee.resolveMelee", ported(melee::resolve)),
  /* beforeDamage: factions.signatureDamage, terrainEffects.burnPass, abilities.statusDamage */
  slot("arena.suddenDeath", pending("P-ARENA-1")), slot("ledger.applyLedger", ported(ledger::apply)),
  /* systems x23, feed.flushAnnouncements = ported(credit::flush_announcements) at #5 */
  slot("arena.settle", ported(settle::settle)), slot("projectiles.clearProjectiles", pending("P-COMBAT-2")),

pub const MOVE_MODIFIERS: &[ModSlot]; pub const MOD_SOURCES: &[SrcSlot]; pub const ACTIONS: &[ActionSlot];

```
The lobby, planning and ended phases get their own short tables. update_active becomes `for s in ACTIVE { if let Run::Ported(f) = s.run { f(cx) } }`. Hooks are static fn-pointer chains, not legacy's runtime closure chaining (world.ts:1062). Room-installed telemetry and trace are kept out: P-OPS-3 owns them. A packet ports a system by changing one table entry from Pending to Ported. It never edits step logic.
Tests in crates/rh-sim/tests/schedule.rs:
(1) legacy_order: read packages/server/src/sim/step.ts (the updateActive body) and gameplay.ts (the MODULES order, then each module's install() push and chainHook order), using the extraction this audit prototyped, which yields the 18-phase list above. Assert equality with ACTIVE/MOVE_MODIFIERS/HOOKS `.legacy` names. Legacy is frozen (P-MIG-4), so parsing it is stable.
(2) A cfg(test) trace inside the loop asserts that a step ran exactly the Ported slots, in table order.

proposals.title: Split the sim.rs monolith into system modules over a narrow, borrow-split context (Static / World / Scratch / Events)
proposals.problem: sim.rs (1,868 lines, 47% of rh-sim) holds lobby, inputs, weapons, movement, melee, ledger, credit/bounty, settlement, results, hashing and the type definitions (Event, Player, Secrets, RunResult). Every method takes `&mut self` over the whole Sim. It uses `std::mem::take(&mut self.melee)` / `take(&mut self.ledger)` (sim.rs:972, 1035) only to get around the borrow checker. 8 of 13 ready packets list sim.rs in their exclusive write scope, as will the 17 coarse section-1 mechanics, so 25 items are serialized on one file (backlog README 'Shared-file rule'). PERSIST-2 needs it only for RunResult and NET-1 only for note_lag (sim.rs:825). Legacy already split these concerns into modules (weapons.ts, melee.ts, ledger.ts, arena.ts, feed.ts, movement.ts); the port merged them into one file.
proposals.change:
Target layout (crates/rh-sim/src/):
- sim.rs: facade, at most 300 lines. new, reset_active, add_player, submit, mark_dropped, remove_player, step, checkpoint/restore.
- state.rs: `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone)] pub struct World { clock: Clock, players: Store<Player>, arena_rt: ArenaRt, rng: Streams, ids: IdGen, winner: Option<NameId>, pending_events: Vec<Event> }`.
- static.rs: `pub struct MatchStatic { config: SimConfig, arena: Arena, secrets: Secrets, names: Names }`. Immutable after the match starts.
- scratch.rs: `TickScratch` (SA5).
- events.rs (SA6). rng.rs gains `Secrets` and `Streams` (one Mulberry32 per enum Stream { Order, Spawn, Plan, Teleport, Reward, ... }), so a new C-RNG stream is one enum variant in rng.rs.
- systems/{lobby, inputs, weapons, movement, melee, ledger, credit (bounty, GV, announcements: legacy arena.ts and feed.ts), settle}.rs, each `pub(crate) fn run(cx: &mut Cx)`.
- `pub struct Cx<'a> { pub k: &'a MatchStatic, pub w: &'a mut World, pub s: &'a mut TickScratch, pub ev: &'a mut Vec<Event>, pub pf: &'a mut Pathfinder }`. Disjoint borrows make the mem::take workarounds unnecessary, and each system's needs show in its signature.
- RunResult and GvBreakdown move to results.rs (P-PERSIST-2's real scope). note_lag moves to systems/weapons.rs (P-NET-1).
Migration with parity at every step:
(1) Pure move: `impl Sim` blocks split across files, no logic change. The state_hash code is untouched, so hashes stay bit-identical and a replay recorded before the move verifies after it.
(2) Introduce Cx and convert the systems one module per commit, with parity-report and replay verification each time.

proposals.parity_notes: Step (1) is a mechanical move, checked by identical replay hashes. Step (2) changes borrows only. Evaluation order of every float expression is kept: only the code location changes, not the arithmetic.
proposals.contract_impact: None to the contracts' content. The README shared-file rule changes from 'sim.rs' to 'schedule.rs and state.rs (one-line edits)' (coordinator). Checkpoint JSON field layout changes once (World and MatchStatic nesting), so old checkpoints are not loadable. Replays are unaffected (they store inputs, not Sim).
proposals.value_for_future: Each backlog mechanic becomes a new file plus a table entry, and packets can be built in parallel instead of 'merged one at a time'. Narrow Cx signatures show what a system can touch, which a reviewer needs to check C-OBS, C-RNG and C-INPUT per packet.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Same system boundaries as legacy's modules (weapons, melee, ledger, arena, feed), now with typed, borrow-checked context instead of a global mutable World bag (world.ts:788-870).

proposals.title: Fighter storage for players now and mobs next: shared FighterCore, id-sorted Store with O(log n) lookup and legacy iteration order, typed FighterRef handles, hot/cold split
proposals.problem: All combat code is written against `self.players[i]` with `i: usize` (sim.rs:771-1388). Mobs (P-MOBS-1, about 204 per match) must fight through the same weapons, movement, melee and ledger code: legacy unifies players and mobs as `Combatant` (combatant.ts:14-16, step.ts:256-257). As written, the Rust port would either duplicate every system for mobs or need a rewrite under parity pressure. Every lookup is a linear scan: idx() (sim.rs:507) is called from 20 sites. rank_of (sim.rs:1023) scans inside a sort comparator (sim.rs:1105), so the ledger is O(E log E * n). apply_ledger calls idx twice per entry (sim.rs:1049), and owed_bounty scans bounty_at_tick_start (sim.rs:1247). Player is one 600-byte struct mixing public body fields, the weapon state machine, inputs and budget, kill-credit bookkeeping, GV and resolution (sim.rs:282-325), so no system has a narrow view and observe() can reach everything.

proof.metric: Lookup cost and ledger scaling vs fighter count; parity; code reuse for mobs
proof.method: (1) Synthetic scaling benchmark available now: a cfg(feature="bench") constructor that places N brawling fighters past MAX_PLAYERS (the cap stays in the real API), driven by rh_policy Brawler for 600 ticks at N = 8, 32, 128, 212. Callgrind Ir per step divided by N, before vs after. (2) Lookup microbench: Store::get vs linear idx at n = 8 and 212 (Ir per lookup). (3) parity-report and parity-bench Ir at N = 8.
proof.expected: Before: Ir per step per fighter grows with N (O(n) idx in 20 sites, rank_of in the sort comparator). After: about flat per fighter for the lookup-bound parts. At n = 212 an average lookup drops from about 106 compares to about 8. At N = 8, parity-bench within +/-1% (binary search over 8 is a wash). Parity 13/13 MATCH.

proposals.parity_notes: Iteration order is unchanged: legacy Map insertion order = join order = id order, and removal is order-preserving. The sortedness invariant is asserted in debug. Action order still shuffles the same join-order id list (sim.rs:728-729).
proposals.contract_impact: None on the wire (PlayerId keeps its u32 value). The checkpoint layout changes, same as SA2.
proposals.value_for_future: P-MOBS-1, P-FACTION-3 (zombies) and P-ARENA-2 (dummies) plug mobs into existing weapons, movement, melee and ledger code through FighterRef. Lookups stay O(log n) at about 212 fighters, and the per-component split gives each later packet (statuses, cards, vision) its own component field instead of more Player fields.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Keeps the Combatant idea and legacy iteration order. Drops string-keyed Maps and the PlayerState/PlayerRuntime pair (world.ts:235-278) with dozens of lazily created optional fields.

proposals.title: State hash derived from the serialized World (checkpoint coverage = hash coverage) with a generic leaf-perturbation test and word-wise mixing
proposals.problem: state_hash (sim.rs:1533-1665) is a 130-line hand-written field list. The only guard is a 9-mutation test (sim.rs:1805-1844). An exhaustive leaf-perturbation probe found 66 of 339 serialized leaves invisible to the hash. Among them: Player.name, which feeds by_name -> killed_by in RunResult (sim.rs:1010, 1217) and the winner (sim.rs:1467). Also queued input contents (mv x/y/seq, move_before, aim_before), config.pvp_rules, secrets and spawns. Checkpoints meanwhile serialize per-tick scratch that is never hashed (rank, bounty_at_tick_start, ledger, melee, stepping: sim.rs:406-410). Every backlog packet has to remember to extend the list by hand (P-COMBAT-1 Acceptance 5, P-COMBAT-3 trap on -Infinity). The hasher is FNV-1a one byte at a time with a 64-bit multiply per byte (sim.rs:1747-1752): 8,873 Ir per call for 4 players, about 0.8x a whole 8-player step, paid every step whenever a match is recorded (replay.rs:108). It grows linearly with every new component and every mob.
proposals.change:
New crates/rh-sim/src/hash.rs with `struct HashSer(u64)` implementing serde::Serializer. It feeds u64-sized words (f64 via to_bits, ints widened, length-prefixed seqs and strings, enum variant index) into a word-at-a-time mixer: one multiply plus xor-shift per word, for example the rapidhash or wyhash folding step written inline, with no new dependency.
`pub fn state_hash(&self) -> u64 { mix(self.k.digest, hash_of(&self.w)) }`, where `MatchStatic::digest` = hash_of(config, arena spawns, map layer_hash, secrets) is computed once at construction. All per-tick scratch lives in `#[serde(skip)] TickScratch` (SA5), so what a checkpoint restores and what the hash sees are the same set by construction. Presentation-only fields (InputQueue.dropped) are `#[serde(skip)]` with a stated reason, or carried in a non-hashed side struct.
Add clippy `disallowed-types = ["std::collections::HashMap", "std::collections::HashSet"]` for rh-sim: their iteration order would make the serialized hash nondeterministic, and BTreeMap or Vec are required instead.
Add crates/rh-sim/tests/hash_coverage.rs, a generalization of this audit's probe: run a scripted match, serialize World, perturb every leaf, deserialize, and assert the hash changed (no allow-list beyond documented skips). Bump REPLAY_FORMAT to rh-replay/2, because hash values change once.

proof.metric: Unhashed leaves; Ir per state_hash call; determinism
proof.method: (1) hash_coverage test: count of perturbed leaves with an unchanged hash. (2) callgrind --toggle-collect='*state_hash*' over 10,000 calls on the same 4-player mid-match state as the baseline, plus a 212-fighter synthetic state. (3) rh-headless/tests/env.rs, rh-server/tests/equivalence.rs and replay round trips stay green. (4) Mutation check: add a dummy field to Player without touching hash code, and hash_coverage must stay green because coverage is automatic. Delete a serde attribute instead, and it must fail.
proof.expected: Unhashed leaves 66 -> 0, except documented #[serde(skip)] presentation fields. Ir per call <= 1/3 of 8,873 for 4 players (word-wise instead of byte-wise multiplies), and linear in state size. C-DET tests green. Gameplay unchanged.

proposals.parity_notes: The hash is an observer, so gameplay and fixtures are unaffected. Recorded replays under rh-replay/1 are invalidated by the format bump, which run_replay rejects cleanly through the format check. The hash now mixes in secrets: keep it server-private, as today, since it is never sent (room.rs:627 is internal).
proposals.contract_impact: C-DET: the hash definition changes and the replay format becomes rh-replay/2 (coordinator updates CONTRACTS.md and MIGRATION.md). No wire or protocol change. The content hash is unaffected.
proposals.value_for_future: No packet can forget hash or checkpoint coverage. A new component is covered the moment it is a serde field of World, which is also the only way it survives a checkpoint. Recording every live match (P-OPS-6 private replay store) stops costing about one extra step of CPU per tick and stays cheap with about 212 fighters.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy had no state hash. This replaces the Stage-1 hand list.

proposals.title: Per-tick scratch arena (not state), allocation-free ledger types shaped for the full legacy ledger, deferred payouts as data
proposals.problem: Per-tick working sets are rebuilt on the heap every step and stored inside the serialized Sim: standing (sim.rs:739), mults (742), join (728), action_order to_vec (rng.rs:32), rank (730), bodies (976), settle alive (1393), ledger victims/idxs/amounts/order/hits (1040-1115). mem::take on melee and ledger (972, 1035) throws away their capacity every tick. Each ledger entry and each hit clones the attacker's name String (sim.rs:1010, 1112). Measured: 14.9 allocations per step, 34.9% of crowded_8 step Ir in allocator/copy/RawVec code. The ledger Entry (sim.rs:372-379) is player-only (victim and by: PlayerId) and stagger-only. Legacy's LedgerEntry (world.ts:389-426) carries a DamageSource with owner, an optional weapon, ability, dot, projectile, scale, sig, passive, arena, derived, final and execute fields, plus a deferred queue and payLater closures. P-COMBAT-2, P-FACTION-1, P-STATUS-1 and P-ARENA-1 would each reshape this struct and its consumers inside sim.rs.
proposals.change:
`#[derive(Default)] pub(crate) struct TickScratch { order: Vec<EntityId>, rank: Vec<u32> /* by slot */, bounty_at_start: Vec<u32> /* by slot */, standing: Vec<FighterRef>, mults: Vec<f64>, melee: Vec<MeleeReq>, ledger: Vec<LedgerEntry>, deferred_next: Vec<LedgerEntry> /* legacy combat.deferred, survives one tick, so it is World state */, victims: Vec<EntityId>, hits: Vec<Hit>, payouts: Vec<Payout>, alive: Vec<EntityId> }`. It is held as `#[serde(skip)]` and cleared with .clear(), never take(). action_order writes into a caller buffer.

proposals.title: Event visibility and delivery class declared on the event itself (exhaustive), and a type-restricted public view for observe
proposals.problem: Event (sim.rs:155-204) lives in sim.rs. Its delivery class `is_important` (sim.rs:207-217) is never called anywhere in the workspace. observe() filters events with a `_ => {}` wildcard (observe.rs, last arm of the event match), and rh-server/src/wire.rs:104 and :131 classify SeenEvent again with `_ => None`. So a packet that adds an Event variant (projectile launch, status applied, chest offer: dozens across the backlog) compiles and is silently dropped for every client and policy. proposals.title: Allocation-free steady-state tick: per-tick working buffers (TickScratch) owned by Sim, plus step_into and swap-drained inputs
proposals.problem: Every active tick does about 15 heap allocations inside Sim::step: 14.89 blocks/step on crowded_8, 9.09 on duel_chase, 9.46 headless. Another 4.36/step happen on the submit path. Allocator code is about 26% of step Ir on crowded_8 and about 37% on duel_chase. Sites: join/order/rank at sim.rs:728-730 and rng.rs:32; standing/mults at sim.rs:739-752; bodies at sim.rs:976; melee and ledger are mem::taken at sim.rs:972/1035, which drops their capacity, so they regrow at :941/:1011; Entry.by_name String clones at sim.rs:1010/1112; victims/mults/idxs/amounts/order/hits at sim.rs:1040-1112; settle's alive Vec at sim.rs:1393; step() returns take_events() at sim.rs:643-657, so the next emit reallocates; InputQueue::drain mem::takes actions at input.rs:157, so push_action at input.rs:147 regrows every tick; plan_path allocates its output plus tile_path and cand at pathfind.rs:126/204/220/239. Each of these scales with entity count once ~204 mobs, projectiles and statuses join the ledger.
proposals.change: Add a #[serde(skip)] Default `Scratch`/`TickScratch` struct to Sim holding the per-tick Vecs (order, actions, path, standing, mults, bodies, victims, ledger mults, idxs, amounts, ord, hits, payouts). Systems take() a buffer, fill it with clear()+extend, and put it back. Restore melee/ledger/downed_this_tick capacity after processing instead of dropping it. Use action_order_in_place over the reused order buffer and keep rank in a reused Vec. Drop Entry.by_name: within one step every ledger source is a present player whose name cannot change, so look the name up at kill time. When projectiles arrive (P-COMBAT-2), carry a Copy NameId or an interned Arc<str> instead of a String. settle counts alive and only collects ids on the end-run path. Add Sim::step_into(&mut Vec<Event>) (out.append(&mut self.events)) and keep step() as a wrapper. InputQueue::drain_into swaps the actions buffer with a scratch buffer, and a clear() covers the lobby/ended/drop paths. Add plan_path_into(.., &mut Vec<Vec2>) and swap the result into p.path. Use sort_unstable_by_key((rank, j)), which gives the stable order with no merge buffer past 20 hits (mob crowds). Optionally make history a VecDeque, which removes the remove(0) memmove at sim.rs:1738 (2.7% of the optimized crowded step). Tick order and every f64 expression are unchanged.

proposals.title: Pathfinder: generation-stamped O(explored) reset, AoS node, precomputed per-tile step mask, scratch outputs, memoized string-pull end discs
proposals.problem: pathfind.rs:49-58 resets g (25,600 f64) and closed (25,600 u8) on every search. On seed1 that costs 44.8k Ir per search, 37% of all find_path cost in rh-headless, where searches expand only about 63 nodes, and 16.9% of the chase workload (41.7M of 247.5M Ir). The astar inner loop at pathfind.rs:144-159 does 4 bounds checks plus up to 3 tile loads per neighbour. The string pull at pathfind.rs:241-246 calls segment_clear, which recomputes circle_clear(anchor) and circle_clear(cand[j]) for every tested j: 56,664 circle_clear calls for 28,332 segment tests in the chase, 50,849 for 25,956 on the 300-query fixture. Output, tile_path and cand Vecs are allocated per query (pathfind.rs:126/220/239).
proposals.change: (a) Store Node{g: f64, parent: i32, stamp: u32} with base += 2 per search: stamp == base means touched (g valid), base+1 means closed, anything else is stale (g = inf, open). Clear fully only when the u32 wraps. (b) Derive TileMap.nav: Vec<u8> at build/rebuild, like comps: bit d set when the DX/DY[d] step is legal, including the diagonal corner rule. The inner loop then tests one byte and keeps the d order. (c) Add find_path_into(.., out: &mut Vec<Vec2>) with tile_path, cand and cand_clear kept in the Pathfinder. (d) In the string pull, compute circle_clear(anchor) once per anchor and memoize circle_clear(cand[j]) per candidate, then run only the ray part (segment_rays_clear). Pure predicates make this exact. Keep the binary heap and before() exactly as they are: the 1e-9 epsilon comparator is not transitive, so heap shape is part of the semantics, and a d-ary heap or bucket queue could reorder near-ties. Keep the PULL_WINDOW linear scan from the far end: clearness is not monotonic in j, so a binary search would change results. Also reset scratch in Sim::clone; today every clone copies the ~333 KB Pathfinder.

proof.metric: callgrind Ir per query or per tick; waypoint bit-equality
proof.method: Prototype in scratch. bench paths check (300 legacy queries, waypoints compared via to_bits) and bench chase check (4 seed1 matches, per-tick state_hash plus events) both pass. Ir: valgrind --tool=callgrind --toggle-collect='bench::pf_b' bench paths opt 1, and --toggle-collect='bench::step_b' bench chase opt parity/maps/seed1.map.json 4 3000, against the orig variants.
proof.expected: Measured: the paths fixture goes from 192.7M to 158.7M Ir with (a)+(c)+(d)+SH3/SH5 (-17.7%) and to 148.9M with (b) as well (-22.7%). The chase goes from 247.5M to 178.1M (-28.0%) and then to 167.7M (-32.3%). circle_clear calls fall from 56,664 to 20,821. Reset cost becomes O(1) instead of O(map), so headless short searches should lose about 44.8k Ir each: about -37% of find_path in rh-headless. For mobs, prove it with the chase bench scaled to more searchers (synthetic); the expectation is that per-search cost tracks nodes expanded, not map size.

proposals.parity_notes: Pushes, pops and comparisons are identical, and the d loop order is preserved. Stamps reproduce the inf/closed semantics exactly. Verified bit-identical on the 300-query legacy fixture and per tick on the chase. Hazard tiles or gates added later must invalidate nav, the same way comps is rebuilt.
proposals.contract_impact: None on the wire. TileMap gains a serde-skipped derived table that is rebuilt in after_restore/start_sim, like comps. Memory: AoS is 16 B/cell, 410 KB on 160x160 versus 333 KB today. Keeping stamp as a separate u32 SoA array gives the same size.

With O(map) resets that is about 45k Ir of dead work per search times hundreds of searches; O(explored) keeps the per-tick path budget meaningful.

proposals.title: Integer floor/ceil helpers in place of software f64::floor/ceil on the tile-index hot paths
proposals.problem: The default x86_64 target has no SSE4.1, so `(v / TILE).floor() as i64` calls the compiler-builtins software floor; callgrind shows the symbol compiler-builtins/.../libm/src/math/generic/floor.rs:floor. Sites: geometry.rs:27-28, 135-136 (plus ceil at :140 and :176), map.rs:145 world_to_tile, rng.rs:37 action_order, sim.rs:685 spawn shuffle. It costs 0.87M Ir (2.2%) of the crowded_8 step and 2.9M (3.3%) of rh-headless.
proposals.change: Add math::floor_i64(v) = { let t = v as i64; if (t as f64) > v { t.saturating_sub(1) } else { t } } and ceil_i64 to match. Both are equal to `v.floor() as i64` / `v.ceil() as i64` for every f64, including NaN (0), ±inf and out-of-range saturation. Use `as usize` for the non-negative Fisher-Yates draw. Portable: aarch64 already has native frintm, and this avoids raising the x86 baseline. Do not swap in `-C target-cpu`.

proof.metric: Ir of the floor symbol; equality property
proof.method: In the prototype: bench floor 20000000 compared helper and std over 60,000,044 values (random bit patterns, values in the tile range, near-integers, and edge values ±0, ±MIN_POSITIVE, 2^52±0.5, ±2^63, ±9.3e18, ±MAX, ±inf, NaN) and found them identical. Keep this as a unit/property test in rh-sim.
proof.expected: The floor symbol disappears from step profiles: about -2% Ir on crowded_8 and about -3% on headless. It is already included in the SH1/SH2 bundle numbers.

proposals.parity_notes: Integer results are mathematically identical for all inputs (verified exhaustively on edges plus 60M samples). No f64 value changes.
proposals.contract_impact: None.
proposals.value_for_future: Every future grid query (vision memory, terrain, projectile sweeps, mob broadphase) converts world to tile; this keeps that conversion at a few instructions on the baseline target.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Math.floor in V8 is a single instruction; a literal port lost that on the default Rust target.

proposals.title: Word-wise state hash (one mix per u64, strings in 8-byte chunks) with a replay format bump
proposals.problem: Sim::state_hash (sim.rs:1533-1666) feeds Fnv64 (sim.rs:1742-1765) one byte at a time: 8 xor-multiply rounds per u64, and str() spends a whole u64 (8 rounds) per character. Recorder::stepped calls it after every step (replay.rs:108), as do run_replay (replay.rs:170), live rooms with record=true and the equivalence tests. Measured cost is 17,139 Ir per tick with 8 players, against 7,609 Ir for Sim::step: recording makes the tick 3.25x as expensive. History and path entries grow it further, and mobs will multiply it.
proposals.change: Keep the exact field list; the_state_hash_sees_every_outcome_field still guards coverage. Replace the byte loop with one mix per 64-bit word: an FxHash-style h = (h.rotl(5) ^ v) * K, or a stronger per-word mixer such as a splitmix64 finalizer if diffusion matters for divergence bisection. Hash strings as their length plus 8-byte little-endian chunks. Bump REPLAY_FORMAT to rh-replay/2, because stored per-step hashes change. Optionally add a debug-only cheap mode for long soak runs.

proof.metric: Ir per state_hash call
proof.method: Prototype: the same traversal made generic over the hasher. valgrind --tool=callgrind --toggle-collect='bench::hash_fnv' versus 'bench::hash_word' with bench hash 1000, on the crowded_8 state after 40 steps. Re-run rh-headless --replay-out under callgrind and read Recorder::stepped.
proof.expected: Measured: 16,181 down to 2,762 Ir per call (-82.9%). The recorded tick should fall from about 24.8k to about 10.4k Ir (step plus hash), and the replay and equivalence tests run about 2-3x fewer instructions.

proposals.parity_notes: Not gameplay: the hash only observes state. Nothing persisted depends on the old values; all hash comparisons in tests are runtime-to-runtime (crates/rh-headless/tests/env.rs, crates/rh-server/tests/equivalence.rs).

proposals.value_for_future: Per-tick determinism hashing stays affordable for live recording and CI soak once ~204 mobs and projectiles enter the hashed state. Byte-wise FNV would grow to several times the step cost.
proposals.legacy_carryover: New in the port (legacy has no per-tick hash); its first implementation chose the slowest FNV variant.

proposals.title: Hit-only ray query (ray_blocked) for every line-of-sight caller; keep raycast for future projectile sweeps
proposals.problem: geometry.rs:18-119 raycast computes len with sqrt and the edge point (ex/ey: a multiply-add, plus branches) on every grid crossing, but all four callers only read .hit: melee LOS (sim.rs:1005), vision (observe.rs:99, which is 34,928 calls and 11.36M Ir, 13% of rh-headless) and the three rays per segment_clear (geometry.rs:165/181/184).
proposals.change: Add ray_blocked(map, x0, y0, x1, y1, mask) -> bool. It is the same DDA with the same t_max divisions and the same corner-squeeze test, and returns at the same decision points. The zero-length test becomes dx*dx+dy*dy == 0.0, which is identical to sqrt(..) == 0.0 including underflow. Use it in segment_clear, melee and observe; keep raycast for P-COMBAT-2 projectile hit points.

proof.metric: Ir per ray; decision equality
proof.method: Prototype: segment_clear switched to ray_blocked and checked bit-identical on the 300 path queries and per tick on the chase. proof.expected: Measured: 894 down to 753 Ir per ray in the string-pull workload (-16%). Expect a similar 10-20% cut of observe's raycast share in rh-headless and wirebench, and of melee LOS (243 Ir/ray in crowded_8).

proposals.parity_notes: Same traversal and same comparisons; only the unused hit point is dropped. Verified via segment_clear on all path fixtures.
proposals.contract_impact: None.

proposals.title: Allocation-free policy drive: observe_into a reused Observation, decide into a buffer, no per-tick event clone
proposals.problem: After SH1, the headless and live tick still allocates about 5.7 blocks per tick outside the sim. Sites: observe.rs:143 visible collect (3.66/tick); observe.rs:147 seen Vec (0.69/tick); Policy::decide returns a fresh Vec (Brawler 0.50/tick, rh-policy lib.rs:123); Env and Room clone the whole event list each tick (headless lib.rs:141, room.rs:523; 775k Ir per 6,000 ticks); results Vecs at lib.rs:143. Each seat also does two linear Sim::player scans (rh-policy lib.rs:162, observe.rs:104; 48,000 calls, 1.75M Ir). drive_seats_with is 5,773 Ir/tick, 41% of the headless tick.
proposals.change: Add observe_into(sim, viewer, events, &mut Observation), which clears and refills visible and events; each Seat owns its Observation. Either add Policy::decide_into(&mut self, obs, out: &mut Vec<RawCommand>) with a default that wraps decide (no contract break), or change decide and bump POLICY_CONTRACT_VERSION. Env and Room keep last_events as the step_into buffer from SH1 and clone only when an external StepOut needs owned events. Resolve the viewer's slot once per seat. Observation content and order (sorted by id) are unchanged.

bugs.description: meanStepUsPerMatchP50 divides the wall time of the whole run_bot_match by ticks. That covers Env::new (arena clone, map rebuild), observe for every seat, policy decisions and the event clone, not just Sim::step. docs/MIGRATION.md:103-105 reports it as a per-step cost ("p50 per-match mean step 14.1 µs", "2.7 µs/step"). Callgrind shows Sim::step is only 54% of Env::step on seed1, so the label overstates the simulation's cost. Documentation and metric mislabel, not a gameplay defect.

The benchmarks are described as "Release builds; x86_64, native", but the repository has no .cargo/config.toml and [profile.release] sets no target-cpu. The release binaries profiled here call the compiler-builtins software floor in the hot path, which a native (SSE4.1) build would not. Either the published numbers came from a different configuration than the shipped build, or the label is wrong. Low impact: about 2-3% of step Ir.

proposals.title: One allocation per viewer-tick: reusable Observation (observe_into) plus streaming snapshot encoder
proposals.problem: Each viewer-tick builds three representations: Observation with Vec<ActorView> and Vec<SeenEvent> (observe.rs:122-145, :147), then ServerMsg with Vec<WireActor> (wire.rs:62-76), then Vec<u8>. The room re-allocates all of them per human per tick (room.rs:553-584). can_see is a linear scan over visible for every event (observe.rs:146), O(E x V) once mobs emit events.
proposals.change: (a) rh-sim: observe_into(&Sim, PlayerId, &[Event], &mut Observation) clears and refills the caller's buffers; observe() becomes a wrapper, so policies keep the same contract. Event filtering uses a per-call visible-id bitset or merge on the sorted ids instead of a linear any(). (b) rh-protocol: a SnapshotWriter (begin(tick, server_ms, phase, ack, Option<&WireSelf>, n) / actor(&WireActor) / finish()); ServerMsg::encode for Snapshot and Fx calls the same functions, so there is one byte layout. (c) rh-server/wire.rs: encode_snapshot(&Observation, ack) -> Vec<u8> maps ActorView to WireActor element by element on the stack (WireActor is Copy), with no Vec<WireActor>. The room keeps one Observation per human; drive_seats keeps one per Seat.

proposals.title: Exact two-disc clearance prefilter for line-of-sight (skip the raycast when the segment provably touches no sight-blocking tile)
proposals.problem: Per-viewer raycasts dominate observation: 26.04M of the 43.41M observe Ir in wirebench (517 Ir/ray), and 69.12M of 110.6M in the 204-mob synthetic. A spatial index does not reduce this cost. The candidate distance test is cheap, and the raycast is what costs (observe.rs:95-100).
proposals.change: At map load, store per tile clr[t] = a lower bound on the distance from any point of tile t to the nearest MASK_SIGHT or out-of-bounds tile, computed with a linear-time EDT on tile centres as max(0, EDT - sqrt(2)) x TILE, capped at VISION_RADIUS. In sees(): if |b - a| < clr[tile(a)] + clr[tile(b)], the line is clear without a raycast. Why this is exact: every point of the segment lies inside one of the two open discs, so every tile the trace enters, including both corner-squeeze neighbours, is within the discs, so none is blocked. NaN distances fall through to the raycast. Keep it as a boolean helper (los_clear) usable by any caller that needs only `hit`, never the hit point. Share the table per map with Arc.

proof.method: (1) Property test over every pinned map: for 10^6 random pairs, prefilter-true implies !raycast(...).hit (scratch: 0 violations in 2M pairs, two-disc fires on 38.2%). (2) A synthetic scaling bench in the repo (port of owbench scale: 204 and 1000 actors, 8 viewers) with callgrind, asserting identical visible-set hashes. (3) callgrind on Env::new for the table build.
proof.expected: Rays -42% at 204 mobs (18.41 -> 10.70 per viewer-tick), -35% at 1000; raycast Ir -29%; identical visible sets; table build < 5M Ir per map (the naive ring search measured 578M, which is not acceptable)

Note that legacy vision LOS is sightLine/hasVisionLineOfSight (packages/shared/src/vision.ts:6-89), not raycast. When P-VISION-1 ports it, the same prefilter stays valid, because sightLine also fails only on a blocked traversed or corner tile, a wall origin, or an out-of-bounds end.
proposals.contract_impact: None (C-OBS results unchanged).
proposals.value_for_future: Scales with the number of visible actors per viewer (mobs, the vision trail) and is reusable by mob aggro and ranged LOS checks that need only a boolean. Legacy already accelerates its vision traces (fastSightLine with FAST_MARGIN fallback, vision.ts:27-53); this is the exact analogue for the boolean query.

proposals.title: Snapshot v2: drop the redundant server_ms, quantize remote actors, delta against the last snapshot WRITTEN to this connection (encoded in the writer task)
proposals.problem: Each Snapshot carries server_ms f64 (lib.rs:457), which always equals tick x 50 (sim.rs:644-645), so 8 of the 89.8 mean bytes are redundant. Remote actors cost 22 B (f32 x/y/facing, u32 id; lib.rs:461-472) and are resent in full every tick although x/y change on only 18% of actor-ticks on the slice. Estimate with the 204-mob synthetic (current sight): 7.4 KB/s per player in snapshots alone. After P-VISION-1 (30 s trail, VISION_TRAIL_MS in packages/shared/src/constants.ts:71), visible counts multiply, and at 1000 actors it is 31 KB/s, above legacy's 11.18/15.17 KB/s and its 20 KB/s gate. The room also encodes a snapshot that latest-wins may then discard (outbox.rs:226-236).
proposals.change: PROTOCOL_VERSION 2. Snapshot = tag, tick u32, phase, ack_input, flags (full/delta), self as a field-mask u16 plus changed fields (keeps f32 x/y for prediction), then actor records: id (u16 or LEB128 varint), field mask u8, changed fields only, with x/y as u16 at 1/8 u (5120 u world; documented 8191 u limit), facing u8, hp_pct, status, weapon, bounty; a list of departed ids. The baseline is the last snapshot this connection's writer task actually wrote. WebSocket over TCP is reliable and ordered, so no ack is needed, and Welcome/resume resets the baseline (full frame). The outbox holds the structured quantized state (latest-wins); the writer task encodes the delta at dequeue, so skipped snapshots are never encoded and encoding leaves the room task. New fields (mob kind, statuses) become new mask bits. Clients derive ServerMs = Tick x 50.

bugs.description: On a catch-up wake (pacer.due returns 2-3 steps, MAX_CATCHUP=3, pacer.rs:10), the events of every step are accumulated (room.rs:523-524) and filtered by ONE observation taken after the last step (room.rs:553). Fx/Swing/Hit/Death events from an earlier step are therefore judged against the viewer's FINAL line of sight. A swing made while the attacker was behind a wall is sent if the attacker steps into view on the next step (a small C-OBS leak), and a death that was visible at its step is dropped if the corpse is out of sight by the final step. Fix: filter each step's events with that step's visibility (observe or the visible-id set per step; cheap, since it happens only on late wakes), then send one Snapshot for the final state.

The encoder writes `actors.len() as u16` without enforcing MAX_ACTORS (512), which the decoders enforce (lib.rs:584; C# Messages.cs uses Wire.MaxActors). An observation with more than 512 visible actors would produce a frame every client rejects as malformed. Above 65,535 it would silently truncate the count and corrupt the frame. Not reachable with 8 players, but reachable once mobs, corpses or chests are actors and the 30 s vision trail widens sight. Encode should clamp, split or debug-assert, and observe should cap with a deterministic rule.
Not a correctness bug, an efficiency defect listed for visibility (see OW3): observations are built for seats whose cadence makes decide() discard them; 63.5% of rh-headless observations are wasted.

keep: Keep the brute-force O(viewers x actors) candidate scan in observe. A uniform interest grid measured no gain at 204 mobs x 8 viewers (110.73M vs 110.60M Ir) and -3% at 1000 mobs: the raycast, not the distance test, is the cost. Mob AI does not observe through observe() (P-MOBS-1: mobs use the sim input path, ADR 0005), so viewers stay at 8 or fewer. Reuse a sim spatial index only if P-MOBS-1 builds one for aggro or hit queries.

Do not share visibility symmetrically between pairs. 0 of 2M random pairs were asymmetric, but raycast symmetry is not proven, legacy vision is directional (isInVision from the viewer), and once mobs dominate the pairs are player->mob, so the saving shrinks to 28 or fewer player-player rays per tick.
Keep rh-protocol independent of rh-sim (the server maps types); OW2 keeps that by giving rh-protocol a streaming writer, not sim types.
Keep the Outbox priority and slow-client isolation design (important never dropped, fx capped, latest-wins snapshot, TooSlow close); OW5 only changes what the snapshot slot holds.
Keep the golden-vector discipline: Rust, C# and v1.json byte equality caught any drift, and it makes OW1/OW2 provably byte-identical.
Keep sorting visible actors by public id (C-OBS). It makes merge-joins possible on the client (OW6) and gives the delta encoder (OW5) a stable order.

proposals.title: state_hash: exhaustive by construction, word-at-a-time, length-prefixed (rh-replay/2)
proposals.problem: Sim::state_hash (crates/rh-sim/src/sim.rs:1533-1665) is a field list kept by hand. A field added by a new mechanic (statuses, items, mobs, quests) and not hashed fails silently. The only guard, the_state_hash_sees_every_outcome_field (sim.rs:1774), is a second hand list of 9 mutations. Gaps today: Player.name, InputQueue contents (only lengths, sim.rs:1638-1642), gv_parts.win/total, ArenaRt.bounty_at_tick_start. They are safe only because queues are empty after a step and name == profile. path and history are not length-prefixed (sim.rs:1561-1569). The hash is also expensive: FNV-1a byte by byte (sim.rs:1691-1712) does 8 multiplies per word, and strings cost one u64 (8 multiplies) per byte. It measures 17,139 Ir per call against 7.6k Ir for the step it fingerprints, and it is 67% of run_replay. At about 38 Ir per hashed word, ~204 mobs at ~25 words each would add about 194k Ir per recorded tick.
proposals.change: (1) Hash in two steps: `let Sim { config: _, arena: _, secrets: _, tick, server_time, ... } = self;` and `let Player { id, profile, name: _ /* == profile */, ... } = p;` with no `..`, repeated for WeaponRt, InputQueue, ArenaRt, GvBreakdown and PendingAction. Adding a field then fails to compile until someone hashes it or writes `_` with a reason. (2) Replace Fnv64::u64 with one xor-multiply(odd)-rotate per word, and hash strings in 8-byte chunks. Every step is still a bijection of the running state, so a single changed word always changes the result, the same guarantee FNV-1a gives. (3) Length-prefix every variable-length list. (4) Add a generic test: serialize sampled Sims (a bot match plus the crowded_8 fixture) to serde_json::Value, perturb every leaf one at a time, deserialize, and assert that state_hash changes unless the JSON path is on an explicit allowlist (config, arena, secrets, events except Resolved, inputs.dropped, ...). A serialized field that is not hashed then fails automatically. (5) Bump REPLAY_FORMAT to rh-replay/2. No golden hashes or replays are checked in (grep: only equality comparisons in env.rs, equivalence.rs and sim.rs).

proof.metric: Ir per state_hash call; Ir of run_replay; compile failure on a new unhashed field
proof.method: callgrind on `rh-headless --matches 1 --players 8 --map parity/maps/seed1.map.json --max-ticks 3000 --replay-out X` and `rh-headless --verify-replay X` (add both as perfproof workloads). Add a dummy field to Player and confirm the build fails. The leaf-mutation test fails on purpose when a field is removed from the hash.
proof.expected: Already prototyped in scratch: 17,139 -> 3,178 Ir/call (-81%); run_replay 77.2M -> 35.1M Ir per 3000-tick replay; the recorded headless run drops by about 41.9M Ir. With exhaustive destructuring and length prefixes the cost should stay within 10% of the prototype.

proposals.parity_notes: The hash is not gameplay; parity fixtures do not contain Rust hashes. Behaviour is unchanged. Only the hash values change, hence the format bump.
proposals.contract_impact: C-DET: replay format rh-replay/1 -> rh-replay/2 (the coordinator edits CONTRACTS). No wire or protocol change.
proposals.value_for_future: Each of the ~40 packets adds state. The hash becomes complete by construction and its cost scales at about 3.8 Ir per word instead of 38, so per-tick recording stays affordable with ~204 mobs, projectiles and statuses. That makes always-on live recording a real option.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy has no state hash; this is new infrastructure.

proposals.problem: rh_policy::drive_seats_with (crates/rh-policy/src/lib.rs:159-182) builds a full Observation (two Vecs, a raycast per other actor) for every standing seat on every tick. Seat::decide (lib.rs:111-114) then throws it away when the seat's cadence is not due. In the 3000-tick seed1 match, 12,017 observations are built and only 4,402 are used. The waste is 18% of all instructions and 8.4k allocations. With mobs, observe walks every entity with a raycast, so the waste grows with entity count.

Then add rh_sim::observe_into(&Sim, id, events, &mut Observation) that reuses each seat's visible/seen Vecs, so a due seat allocates nothing. Keep observe() as a wrapper so C-OBS keeps its API.

proposals.problem: InputQueue.actions is a Vec (crates/rh-sim/src/input.rs:109). drain() mem::takes it (input.rs:155), so each tick's first action push reallocates (input.rs:136). This is the largest sim-side allocation site: 15,728 of 125,723 blocks (2.0 MB) in crowded_8, and 1,307 in the headless run. The cap is a constant (MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TICK = 6), so the heap buys nothing.
proposals.change: Store `actions: [ActionCmd; MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TICK]` plus `len: u8` (a hand-written ArrayVec, no new dependency), and have Drained borrow or copy it (6 x 32 B). Serialize it as a sequence of the first len entries so the checkpoint JSON shape stays a list. Arrival order and the >= 6 => QueueFull rule stay identical. (The scratch prototype used a spare-buffer swap with the same effect.)

proposals.title: Compact binary replay (inputs + raw u64 hashes + raw tiles); JSON kept as a debug export
proposals.problem: Replays are JSON (crates/rh-sim/src/replay.rs:62-73; rh-headless main.rs:66). They are 2.9x larger than needed (242,510 B for 3000 ticks, of which 51 KB is the tile layer as a JSON number array and 61 KB is u64 hashes as decimal text). They are slow: decode is 10.25M Ir per 3000 ticks because float_roundtrip parsing is required. Their exactness also depends on a Cargo feature: a binary that deserializes a replay through serde_json without `float_roundtrip` (rh-persist already depends on serde_json without it) may parse some f64 off by one ulp and fail the C-DET check.
proposals.change: Add a pure codec in rh-sim (no I/O: it encodes into Vec<u8>). Header: format tag, content_hash, config, secrets, start, arena as w/h + raw tile bytes (or the layer_hash plus the map file reference) + spawns. Body: tick deltas as varints, input tag + varint player + f64 bit patterns, and hashes as raw LE u64. Same shape as rh-protocol's Writer/Reader. rh-headless --replay-out writes .rhr; --verify-replay accepts both formats; JSON stays available for debugging.

proof.metric: bytes per replay; Ir to encode/decode; exact round trip
proof.method: Scratch microbench sebench (sizes, json-enc/dec, bin-enc/dec under callgrind); a test that round-trips the replay and requires equality plus a successful run_replay
proof.expected: Prototyped: 242,510 -> 83,816 B (-65%); encode 4.36M -> 0.30M Ir; decode 10.25M -> about 0.1M Ir plus the rebuild of derived tables that both paths need; round trip equal and replays verify. Floats are bit-exact by construction, with no reliance on float_roundtrip.

proposals.parity_notes: Storage format only.
proposals.contract_impact: C-DET format: adds rh-replay/2 binary (pairs with SE1's format bump); ADR 0007's 'JSON with float_roundtrip' line is updated.
proposals.value_for_future: Makes always-on recording of live matches (12,000-tick matches, about 0.3 MB binary instead of about 1 MB JSON) and bulk replay verification cheap. Mob and projectile packets add inputs, not per-tick state, so replay size stays proportional to inputs.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy had no replays.

proposals.title: Deserialization completes derived tables (TileMap try_from); delete rebuild()/after_restore
proposals.problem: TileMap.comps is #[serde(skip)] (crates/rh-sim/src/map.rs:22) but decides outcomes (pathfind.rs:208 plan_path compares components). Every deserialization site must remember to call rebuild(): replay.rs:183, rh-headless main.rs:19 (redundant, so it rebuilds twice) and Sim::after_restore (sim.rs:496-499). A missed call panics at map.comp(). A malformed map (tiles.len() != w*h) deserializes fine and later panics in tile(). TileMap derives PartialEq/Hash over comps, so a deserialized Replay is unequal to the original until rebuilt. Sim.pathfinder is already Default under serde(skip), so after_restore's only real job is the map rebuild.
proposals.change: `#[serde(try_from = "TileMapRepr", into = "TileMapRepr")]` on TileMap. try_from calls TileMap::new, which validates the shape and builds comps. Exclude comps from PartialEq/Hash (manual impls over w, h, tiles). Then a deserialized Sim is complete: remove after_restore (or keep it as a deprecated no-op) and the three rebuild() calls. Same for any future derived table (vision grids, spatial index for mobs).

proof.metric: rebuild()/after_restore call sites; behaviour on malformed input
proof.method: grep count 3 -> 0; tests: a checkpoint and a replay deserialize and continue identically with no extra call (env.rs checkpoint test minus the after_restore line); a map with len != w*h returns a serde error instead of panicking; Replay equality holds right after deserialization
proof.expected: 0 manual rebuild sites; malformed map -> Err; existing determinism tests green

proposals.parity_notes: Derived data is computed by the same function at the same moment, before first use.
proposals.contract_impact: C-DET wording ('after_restore rebuilds derived tables') simplifies; the checkpoint JSON shape is unchanged.
proposals.value_for_future: Vision memory, terrain layers and spatial indexes for ~204 mobs will add derived tables. With this pattern a checkpoint can never be restored half-built.

proposals.title: Parity harness: format-based discovery, generic entity-projection compare, unknown keys fail
proposals.problem: (a) fixture_paths (crates/rh-parity/src/lib.rs:451-468) fully parses every *.json in parity/fixtures to read `parity`. The new legacy_schedule.json broke the gate at HEAD (see bugs), and every fixture is parsed twice per run. (b) Per-player state comparison is hand-written: the FixState struct (lib.rs:79-89) plus a block of hard-coded checks (lib.rs:327-370) for six fields. Each mechanic packet (statuses, items, ammo, mobs, chests) must edit the struct, the compare code and the report. Mobs and projectiles are not players at all. (c) FixState/Fixture do not deny unknown fields, so a key newly emitted by capture.ts is silently ignored and the gate reports a false MATCH.
proposals.change: Discover fixtures by a cheap header peek on `format` (rh-legacy-scenario/1), or by a parity/fixtures/manifest.json listing {file, format, parity}. Represent each tick's state as entity maps (`players`, later `mobs`, `projectiles`, ...) of serde_json Values. On the Rust side keep one projection table: (entity kind, key) -> (fn(&Sim, id) -> Value, tolerance class exact|abs TOL|angle). compare() walks the legacy keys. A legacy key with no projection fails as 'unported key K' unless the fixture lists it in `notCompared`. A new mechanic then needs its capture fields plus one projection line. Events are already generic (canon + same_value); keep them.

proof.metric: harness edits per new per-entity field; false-MATCH detection; parse work per gate run
proof.method: (1) The gate is green again with legacy_schedule.json present. (2) Add a synthetic 'barrier' key to a copy of fists_duel.json: today the harness says MATCH; after the change it fails with 'unported key'. (3) Count the code locations a new field touches: 3 today (struct, compare, report) vs 1 projection entry. (4) Callgrind of parity-report: each fixture parsed once instead of twice.

proposals.contract_impact: C-PARITY tooling only; the fixture format gains optional `notCompared` (rh-legacy-scenario/1 stays readable).

The lease row lock is held for about 10 of them. Each match end fans out up to 8 of these concurrently (director.rs:404-439) against a 16-connection pool.

Statement 2: one data-modifying CTE that updates profiles, upserts gv_by_month with to_char(now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM') inline, inserts gv_ledger when gv > 0, inserts match_results and releases the lease. Keep one transaction per (match, profile); do not batch across players, so one profile's failure never blocks another's.

bugs.description: The parity gate is broken at HEAD 79dfba3. fixture_paths deserializes every *.json in parity/fixtures except pathfinding*. The legacy_schedule.json added in 79dfba3 (format rh-legacy-schedule/1, no `scenario`) makes load() panic at lib.rs:118 ('missing field `scenario` at line 443'). `cargo test -p rh-parity` fails every_slice_fixture_matches_legacy, parity-report panics, and the CI clippy/test job is red. Verified fix in a scratch copy: skip non-scenario files (filter on `format == "rh-legacy-scenario/1"`, or exclude legacy_schedule*). After it, all 13 slice fixtures and 300 path queries MATCH.

Fixture, FixState and FixResult lack #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], and compare() checks a fixed field list. A per-tick key newly emitted by capture.ts (for example barrier or statuses in a mechanic packet) is silently ignored and the gate reports a false MATCH. Today every captured key is compared, so this is a latent harness hole (see SE6).

js_round(x) = (x + 0.5).floor() is not JavaScript Math.round. It differs at x = 0.49999999999999994 (JS 0, Rust 1) and for odd integers >= 2^52 (JS 4503599627370497, Rust ...498); checked with node against Python's floor(x + 0.5). It is used by bounty_for (content.rs:157), where values are pow-derived, and for duration (sim.rs:1510, safe domain). Future reward packets will call it on arbitrary f64. Exact fix: `let f = x.floor(); if x - f >= 0.5 { f + 1.0 } else { f }`.

run_replay checks content_hash but never checks `r.format == REPLAY_FORMAT`. A replay written in a later format (needed once the hash function or encoding changes, SE1/SE4) would run as rh-replay/1 and fail with a misleading Diverged error instead of a format error.

state_hash concatenates p.path (2 words per point) and p.history (3 words per sample) without length prefixes. Different (path, history) splits can feed the same word stream. It also omits Player.name, InputQueue contents (only lengths, sim.rs:1638) and gv_parts.win/total. This is correct today only by invariants nothing enforces: queues are drained by every step, name == profile, and parts win/total stay 0. See SE1.

TileMap derives PartialEq/Eq/Hash including the #[serde(skip)] derived `comps`. A deserialized map (and therefore Replay/Arena) compares unequal to the original until rebuild() is called, and tiles.len() != w*h is accepted by serde and panics later in tile() (map.rs:91) or comp() (map.rs:117). See SE5.

keep: rng.rs: mulberry32 is bit-exact with legacy vectors, each stream has one purpose, and action_order is a pure function of (salt, tick, join order). No entropy, no HashMap, no clock anywhere in rh-sim (grep-verified).
math.rs as the single source of libm transcendentals, with sqrt as IEEE and wrap_angle via fmod (exact). No std transcendental is used elsewhere in rh-sim, rh-policy or rh-headless (grep-verified).

One input path: validate + Sim::submit with the order budget on SIM time. The Recorder records every validated command, including budget-refused ones (they move the bucket's refill state), so replays re-submit them. This is correct and should stay.
drive_seats_with is shared by the live room and the headless runner, and the Recorder by both. This is the right seam for the live = headless equivalence (rh-server/tests/equivalence.rs).

Sorts that matter are stable or total: observe sorts by unique id, and apply_victim's sort_by_key(rank) is stable as JS's Array.sort is. Keep stable sorts (or make the key total with the index) in combat ordering.

Persistence semantics: one transaction per (match, profile), idempotent by match_results PK, fenced lease, gv only with a ledger row, retries off the room task with a drain wait. Optimize the round trips (SE9), not the model.
Pathfinder scratch reuse: its results do not depend on earlier searches (g/closed reset per search; parent read only for reached nodes), so restoring it as Default is sound.

proposals.title: Entities by dense handle: no names or string identities in the ledger, O(1) lookups, and a Copy legacy key for tie-breaks
proposals.problem: Legacy identity is a string, and Stage 1 copied the parts of that design that hurt. (1) Names travel with every hit: Entry.by_name: String (sim.rs:375), cloned per ledger entry (sim.rs:1010) and again per hit into Vec<(f64, PlayerId, String)> (sim.rs:1106-1115). killed_by is stored as a name (sim.rs:1217) and winner as a String (sim.rs:401, 1465). This copies ledger.ts sourceOf, which falls back to by.name because removePlayer deletes the fighter (step.ts removePlayer). Rust deletes too (sim.rs:639). (2) Legacy's Map<string,...> lookups became linear scans: idx() (sim.rs:507-509, 23 call sites), rank_of() inside the sort comparator (sim.rs:1023-1029, 1105), owed_bounty's find (sim.rs:1246-1252), victims.contains (sim.rs:1042) and the idxs filter per victim (sim.rs:1059, O(victims x entries)). (3) Legacy ids decide outcomes beyond lookup, and the port will have to reproduce this. tieRank hashes the id's characters (world.ts:1082-1086). Mob order is by id string: mobIdOrder (mobLife.ts:321) and localeCompare (factions.ts:383, 922). nextId (world.ts:1089) uses ONE counter shared by containers, projectiles, fields, mobs and quests (loot.ts:49, projectiles.ts:51, fields.ts:15, mobs.ts:36, quests.ts:91), so firing an arrow changes the next mob's id and therefore its tie rank. tieRank is called inside sort comparators (mobAI.ts:163, consumables.ts:161), which recomputes a hash on every comparison.
proposals.change: (a) Add an append-only per-match Roster: PlayerId -> slot, with SeatInfo{profile, name, bot} kept for leavers. The live players list holds slots. (b) Make ledger Entry, MeleeReq and Payout Copy, with Source = enum {Fighter(slot), Arena, ...} and no String. Resolve names from the roster only when building RunResult; killed_by stays a String there, so the wire and persistence do not change. (c) Use dense per-slot arrays for the tick rank, bounty_at_tick_start and victim grouping (first-appearance index per slot), so every lookup is O(1) and every order is preserved. (d) Add LegacyKey{prefix: u8, n: u32} (8 bytes, Copy), issued by one IdAllocator that mirrors legacy nextId's shared counter at exactly the legacy call sites. tie_rank(salt, tick) writes prefix + base36 digits into a stack buffer. Ord implements mobIdOrder, and a separate cmp gives byte-lexicographic order (localeCompare on [0-9a-z] ids). Compute one tie rank per entity per tick into a dense array instead of hashing inside comparators. Players take their key from the seat: the capture id in parity, the decimal public id live.

proof.metric: String/heap blocks per step and instr per step (crowded_8); exactness of tie_rank and id ordering against legacy; ledger cost scaling with victim count
proof.method: dhat and callgrind on parity-bench crowded_8 (runs 1 vs 3, delta/1802) before and after. cargo run -p rh-parity --bin parity-report. New unit vectors captured from node: tieRank for 1,000 nextId strings x 3 salts x 3 ticks; JS sort order of 5,000 keys under localeCompare and mobIdOrder. Synthetic microbench in a custom CARGO_TARGET_DIR: apply_ledger with 50/100/200 victims and 2 entries each, counting instructions with callgrind
proof.expected: The ~1.86 String-related blocks/step go to 0. Every parity scenario still MATCHes (13 + 300 paths). The legacy vectors match exactly. The synthetic ledger grows roughly linearly instead of quadratically (more than 10x fewer instructions at 200 victims than the current linear scans). At 8 players instr/step is equal or lower

proposals.parity_notes: Keep these orders exactly: victims grouped in first-appearance order; the stable sort by rank (mobs and others at Infinity, after the players); join order for action_order; the leaver-name fallback (a departed shooter is credited by name only, with no GV). The IdAllocator must bump at exactly the legacy nextId sites, in the same order, or tie-breaks diverge. Capture tests make that checkable before mobs land.
proposals.contract_impact: No wire change (RunResult.killed_by stays a String). The checkpoint/replay serde format changes, so old JSON checkpoints cannot be loaded. state_hash must cover the roster. C-INPUT, C-OBS and C-RNG are unchanged; tie_rank uses order_salt exactly as legacy does.
proposals.value_for_future: Mobs (~204), projectiles, containers, fields and quests all need ids, tie ranks and id ordering that match legacy. Designing the allocator and key now puts that parity-critical logic in one tested place instead of 10 packets, and keeps the ledger allocation-free and O(entries) when mob hits multiply its size.
proposals.legacy_carryover: String identity in ledger and results (ledger.ts sourceOf/by.name, world.ts nextId/tieRank, mobLife.ts mobIdOrder, factions.ts localeCompare), with legacy's Map lookups degraded to linear scans

proposals.title: Tick schedule as a declared table, tested against parity/fixtures/legacy_schedule.json
proposals.problem: In legacy the tick order is emergent: it comes from the module install order plus push/unshift into afterWeapons, beforeDamage, systems, moveModifiers and modSources, and from chainHook install order (world.ts:1062-1066). It is resolved only when createGameWorld runs. Stage 1 copied the order as straight-line code with bracketed comments (sim.rs:714-769: '[abilities] [target locks] -- not in the slice', '[beforeDamage: ...]'). Where the 24 production systems, 7 move modifiers, 3 afterWeapons and 3 beforeDamage entries go is therefore recorded only in prose. Example: flush_bounty_announcements (sim.rs:767) is legacy systems entry 6 of 24 (feed.flushAnnouncements). fireRoam.update, factions.afterDamage, factions.healOverTime, mobs.resetDummies and buffs.expireBoosts must be inserted before it, and 18 entries after it. The move-multiplier product is folded left to right in f64 (step.ts updateActive reduce), so its order is behaviour. 8 of 13 ready packets edit sim.rs to insert phases by hand.
proposals.change: Add schedule.rs with enum SystemId listing every updateActive phase and every hook-list entry in legacy production order (from legacy_schedule.json). Each entry carries a config gate (signatures, walkHints, mobs, training...) and a Ported/Unported flag. update_active becomes `for s in ACTIVE { match s { ... } }`. moveModifiers becomes an ordered list folded left to right from moveMultiplierOf, and chained event hooks (hitLanded, playerKilled, mobKilled, campCleared...) become ordered lists. A test in rh-parity loads legacy_schedule.json and asserts that the projection of ACTIVE under the capture config equals the capture lists, and under the production config equals the production lists (verified possible: capture is a subsequence of production for all 5 lists). A mechanic packet then adds a module file and flips an entry from Unported to Ported. Depends on fixing the schedule.ts hook-chain recording (bugs).

proof.metric: Schedule conformance test result; instr/step overhead
proof.method: New cargo test in rh-parity, plus a mutation check: swap two adjacent entries, or move FlushBounty, and the test must fail. Callgrind parity-bench crowded_8 instr/step before and after. parity-report
proof.expected: The test is green on the declared table and red under the mutation. Instr/step stays within +/-2% of 15,245 (about 50 match arms per tick). Every parity scenario MATCHes.

proposals.parity_notes: The order is not changed, only declared. The test makes C-TICK machine-checked instead of a comment. Keep the non-list phases (guard:voided, ledger:openWithDeferred, inputs:mobs(insertionOrder), suddenDeath(notTraining), settle vs settle:training, projectiles:clearIfEnded) as named table entries.
proposals.contract_impact: C-TICK gains an executable check. No wire, observation or determinism change.
proposals.value_for_future: Each of the ~40 packets inserts its systems at a position the test verifies, and parallel packets stop conflicting on hand-edited lines in update_active. Divergence between the production and capture worlds is caught at build time.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Implicit order spread across install calls, push/unshift and chainHook (world.ts, gameplay.ts, step.ts), now spread across comments in sim.rs

proposals.title: Split the single Player record into owned components, share a Fighter core with mobs, use one lifecycle enum, and derive the state hash
proposals.problem: sim.rs:282-325 Player has 43 fields mixing several kinds of state: seat/network (profile, inputs, budget, dropped_at), body (x, y, facing, path, history), vitals (hp, max_hp, barrier, immune_until), weapon runtime, credit/results (gv_parts, damaged, damaged_humans, last_hit, killed_by, announce, bot_kills) and per-tick scratch (hp_frac_at_tick_start). Legacy at least split PlayerState (synced) from PlayerRuntime, and wrapped mobs as Combatant{kind, s, rt} (combatant.ts) so melee, movement and ledger ran over both. Rust merged everything into one record that only a player can be. Every system then goes through &mut Sim, indexes self.players[i] and looks ids up again (e.g. sim.rs:1131 after apply_hits). Lifecycle lives in three overlapping fields, status/down/resolved (standing() at sim.rs:328-330), and some combinations only exist by convention: Alive + resolved means a winner. state_hash (sim.rs:1533-1665) is a 130-line hand list. The exit review already found it missing outcome fields (docs/MIGRATION.md defect 12), it still hashes only counts of queued inputs (sim.rs:1638-1642), and it costs 1.65x the step it checks (17.4k vs 10.6k instr/tick). Part of that is Fnv64::str running 8 multiply rounds per byte (sim.rs:1756-1761).
proposals.change: Fighter{body: Body, vitals: Vitals, combat: Combat(WeaponRt, ready_at, draw_started_at), life: Life} is used by players now and by mobs later. Per player only: Seat{roster slot, inputs, budget, dropped_at} and Credit{kills, bot_kills, bounty, gv_parts, last_hit, damaged, damaged_humans, killed_by, announce}. Life = Lobby | Standing | Down{outcome, resolved} | Winner{resolved}, with the wire Status derived from it. Systems become functions over the components they own: movement gets &mut Body plus &Combat; the ledger gets Vitals plus Credit. Each component implements a StateHash trait (derived or macro-generated, word-oriented mixing), so every serialized field is hashed by construction. An explicit, tested exclusion list covers transients such as scratch, so leaving a field out is a decision, not an omission. History becomes a fixed-capacity ring (8 samples cover MAX_REWIND_MS + TICK_MS; use 9 with a debug assert), so Body is fixed-size.

proof.metric: Hash completeness; state_hash instr per tick; parity and determinism
proof.method: (1) A generic test serializes a mid-match checkpoint to serde_json::Value, perturbs each leaf one at a time, deserializes, and asserts state_hash changes. Run it at HEAD first to list the fields the hand-written hash misses (expected non-empty, e.g. queued Move coordinates and move_before/aim_before), then confirm it passes after the change. (2) Callgrind rh-headless --matches 1 --players 8 --max-ticks 2000 --replay-out: state_hash instr/tick before and after. (3) parity-report, rh-headless/tests/env.rs, rh-server/tests/equivalence.rs
proof.expected: The completeness test lists misses at HEAD and passes after. state_hash drops from ~17.4k to under the step's ~10.6k instr/tick (at least 3x lower with word mixing instead of per-byte u64 rounds). Every parity scenario MATCHes. C-DET tests are green.

proposals.parity_notes: This is a pure data-layout change. Iteration order over fighters must stay join order for players, and insertion order for mobs later (inputs:mobs(insertionOrder)). Hash values change, so recorded replays must be re-recorded; no golden hash is pinned in fixtures.
proposals.contract_impact: C-DET: the state hash definition changes, and checkpoints/replays from before are invalid. C-OBS gets easier to audit, because observations are built from public components only. No wire change (Status is derived). Depends on LC1 (slots).
proposals.value_for_future: P-MOBS-1 (~204 mobs) reuses Body/Vitals/Combat and the movement, melee and ledger code unchanged, with no budgets, profiles or GV attached to mobs. Every packet's new state is hashed automatically, closing the defect class the exit review found, and replay hashing stays affordable at 25x the entity count.
proposals.legacy_carryover: One mutable fighter object touched by every system (legacy PlayerState+PlayerRuntime via Combatant), made worse by merging both into one 43-field record; lifecycle spread over status/down/resolved as in legacy arena.ts

proposals.title: One rules table holding every gameplay number, with content_hash derived from all of it
proposals.problem: content_hash (content.rs:318-371) is documented as the identity of the rules in this build, but it covers 16 of the 36 constants in constants.rs. Not covered: MOVE_MULT_FLOOR, KILL_CREDIT_SECONDS, STAGGER_IMMUNITY_SECONDS, AIM_STALE_MS, TIE_EPS_MS, RANGED_RELEASE_PAUSE_MS, WIN_BONUS_MIN_PLAYERS/OPPONENTS, BOUNTY_FREE_KILLS, BOUNTY_ANNOUNCE_MS, MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TICK, MAX_PLAYERS, ORDER_BURST/PER_SECOND, and the WORLD clamp. Also not covered: the windup formulas (content.rs:309-310: 0.5/0.55, 0.45/0.5) and rules written as code: stagger only for the sword (sim.rs:1017, legacy interactions.ts:77), the Draw kind for the bow (sim.rs:902-906), and the outcome-relevant epsilons (barrier 1e-3 at sim.rs:1193, arc 1e-9 at sim.rs:1689, facing 0.001 at sim.rs:1710). Legacy has the same split: a flat shared/constants.ts, rules in interactions.ts, and per-module consts. The backlog brings 80 cards, 30 mob types, 14 status rules and the MOB_* multipliers.
proposals.change: Add a Rules struct (Serialize, one const instance) holding the faction sheet, the weapon catalog (including the player/NPC timing profiles and a stagger flag), combat, credit, bounty and win-gate numbers, input limits and the documented epsilons. Systems read rules.* instead of free constants. content_hash = FNV over the canonical serialization of Rules, so adding a field adds it to the identity automatically. Pure engineering constants that cannot change outcomes stay outside Rules, with a comment saying why.

proof.metric: Hash sensitivity to every rule number; parity; instr/step
proof.method: Unit test: serde_json::to_value(RULES), perturb each numeric/bool leaf in turn, assert content_hash changes (at HEAD this fails, e.g. for KILL_CREDIT_SECONDS). parity-report. Callgrind parity-bench crowded_8
proof.expected: The test fails at HEAD and passes after. Every parity scenario MATCHes (numbers are unchanged). Instr/step changes by less than 1%.

proposals.parity_notes: The values and evaluation order are unchanged. Only the place the numbers are read from moves. Keep expressions such as `x * 1000.0` and `0.5f64.min(0.55 * interval)` textually identical (C-NUM).
proposals.contract_impact: content_hash changes value once. Welcome and /info carry the new value, and the C# client and browser proof read it from /info. Replays recorded under the old hash are refused, which is the point. No PROTOCOL_VERSION bump and no golden-vector change: fixtures use sample hashes.
proposals.value_for_future: The cards, mob types, statuses and quests become rows in one hashed table instead of scattered consts. A client or replay built against different numbers is always refused at admission or load instead of diverging silently. It also gives tuning and the parity capture one place to diff.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Magic numbers and rules outside the content table (shared/constants.ts bag, interactions.ts staggers/shieldOutcome, inline epsilons)

proposals.title: Time: keep f64 milliseconds (required for parity), but derive the clock from the tick and type the units
proposals.problem: Both tick and server_time are stored, advanced (sim.rs:644-645) and hashed (sim.rs:1535-1536), although server_time always equals tick x 50 exactly (50*k is exact in f64). The seconds-to-ms conversion is hand-written at 8 sites (sim.rs:545, 671, 901, 916, 918, 1260, 1378, 1510), copying legacy's seconds-in-content, ms-in-runtime split. Verdict on integer ticks: do NOT quantize durations. Attack timing is fractional and carries its phase: Fire fists interval = max(0.2, 1/(0.6*2.5)) = 0.6667 s, ready_at = start + 666.67 ms, and start = ready_at.max(now - TICK_MS) (sim.rs:895-899). Rounding to ticks would change attack cadence and break parity.
proposals.change: Add a SimTime newtype (f64 ms, constructible only from a tick count), plus Ms and Secs newtypes where Secs::to_ms() performs the identical `x * 1000.0`. Remove the stored server_time field and derive it. Durations stay f64. Comparisons keep TIE_EPS_MS.

proof.metric: Bit-exactness and compile-time unit safety
proof.method: parity-report; a unit test checking that tick*50.0 equals the accumulated +50.0 sum for 0..10^7 ticks; checkpoint round-trip tests; deliberately mixing Secs and Ms in a compile-fail doc test
proof.expected: All parity scenarios MATCH bit-exactly. The equality test passes for all 10^7 ticks. Unit mix-ups fail to compile.

proposals.parity_notes: The arithmetic is the same operations in the same order. Do not change TIE_EPS_MS handling or the fractional ready_at/lands_at values.
proposals.contract_impact: C-TICK is unchanged (time still advances only through step). The checkpoint format loses a field. State hash values change only if the hashed time field is removed (it can stay as a derived value).
proposals.value_for_future: Statuses, abilities, respawn (180 s), the coliseum schedule and quests multiply the number of second/ms conversions. Typed units stop an off-by-1000 bug, and a single clock removes a class of checkpoint inconsistencies.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Time as f64 ms plus seconds-valued content with manual *1000 at call sites (legacy everywhere)

proposals.title: Replace the TypeScript new-array-per-tick idiom with buffers reused across ticks
proposals.problem: Measured on crowded_8: 19.32 heap blocks and 1,804 B allocated per step. Allocator code takes 4,313 of the 15,245 instr/step (28%). The sources mirror the legacy map/filter/new Map style 1:1. InputQueue::drain hands its Vec away every tick (input.rs:150-162, mem::take), so the next push regrows it: 4.36 allocs/step. Other sources: action_order's to_vec plus the join and rank Vecs (rng.rs:31, sim.rs:728-730); the standing and mults collects (sim.rs:739-752); resolve_melee bodies (sim.rs:976); apply_ledger victims/mults/idxs/payouts (sim.rs:1040-1063); apply_victim amounts/order/hits (sim.rs:1083-1115); settle's alive list (sim.rs:1393); a fresh events Vec on every step (sim.rs:517, 657). History is reset with vec![] (sim.rs:485, 697) and trimmed with remove(0) (sim.rs:1737); the path is consumed with remove(0) (sim.rs:1704). All of these grow with fighter count once mobs arrive.
proposals.change: Add a #[serde(skip)] Scratch struct on Sim holding Vecs that are cleared and reused each tick. InputQueue::drain_into(&mut Drained) keeps capacity. Add step_into(&mut Vec<Event>), or a borrowed events slice that the caller clears. Use a ring buffer for history (shared with LC3) and a cursor for the path, or store the path reversed. after_restore rebuilds the scratch.

proof.metric: Heap blocks per step; instr per step
proof.method: dhat and callgrind on parity-bench crowded_8 (runs 1 vs 3, delta/1802), before and after. parity-report. rh-headless/tests/env.rs checkpoint tests (scratch is not serialized)
proof.expected: Blocks/step fall from 19.3 to at most 1. Instr/step drops 20-30% (most of the 4.3k allocator share). All parity scenarios MATCH.

proposals.parity_notes: Only storage changes. Every iteration order (join order, victim first appearance, rank sort stability) and every float operation stays the same.
proposals.contract_impact: None. A Sim::step signature variant is added for callers (rh-server, rh-headless, rh-parity) that want a borrowed event buffer.
proposals.value_for_future: At ~212 fighters the per-tick collects scale with fighters and hits, and allocator cost would take a growing share of the budget toward the legacy stepBench gate (avg < 5 ms). Reused buffers give a fixed, allocation-free steady state that later packets inherit by convention.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Per-tick fresh arrays and Maps (step.ts updateActive fighters/mults, ledger.ts byVictim Map, InputQueue.drain returning new arrays, history.shift/path.shift)

proposals.title: Uniform-grid broadphase over the fighter store for melee targets and observation candidates (value arrives with mobs)
proposals.problem: resolve_melee tests every standing body for every swing, running position_at + in_arc + raycast per pair (sim.rs:976-1019). observe raycasts every actor for every viewer (observe.rs:97-102, 126-131). Legacy melee is identical (melee.ts:46-62); legacy had no interest management at all. Already with 8 players, observe is 44.6% of rh-headless instructions against 16.1% for Sim::step (callgrind above). With ~204 mobs the bodies per swing and the candidates per viewer grow about 26x.
proposals.change: After recordHistory, rebuild a grid once per tick (cells of 4 tiles) from present positions. Melee queries the cells within reach + PLAYER_RADIUS + R, where R is the maximum distance a body can be from its rewound sample (max speed from Rules x MAX_REWIND_MS, about 51 u plus slack; teleports and displacements reset history, so they stay inside the bound). The candidate slots are then SORTED ascending so bodies are visited in the same order as today. Observe queries the cells within VISION_RADIUS. The grid is scratch, not serialized.

proof.metric: Pair tests and raycast calls per tick vs fighter count; instr per step at N=8
proof.method: Synthetic bench in a custom CARGO_TARGET_DIR, using a test-only constructor that places N = 8, 32, 64, 128, 256 fighters on seed1.map.json, with deterministic raycast/pair counters and callgrind. Also callgrind parity-bench crowded_8 and wirebench --ticks 2000 before and after, and parity-report
proof.expected: Pair and raycast counts grow roughly linearly with local density instead of with N squared (expect more than 10x fewer at N=256). At N=8, instr/step is within +/-3% (no regression). All parity scenarios MATCH.
