bugs.description: content_hash is documented as the identity of the rules in this build (sent in Welcome, checked by run_replay at replay.rs:149-152), but it leaves out 19 gameplay numbers from constants.rs. Among them: KILL_CREDIT_SECONDS, MOVE_MULT_FLOOR, STAGGER_IMMUNITY_SECONDS, AIM_STALE_MS, RANGED_RELEASE_PAUSE_MS, TIE_EPS_MS, WIN_BONUS_MIN_*, BOUNTY_FREE_KILLS, BOUNTY_ANNOUNCE_MS, MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TICK, ORDER_BURST/PER_SECOND and the world clamp. It also leaves out the windup formula numbers (content.rs:309-310) and the stagger-on-sword rule (sim.rs:1017). Changing any of these changes gameplay without changing the hash: a client or replay built on different rules is admitted, or loaded and then diverges, and the failure is reported as a state-hash mismatch instead of a content mismatch.

For each runtime hook, the schedule capture keeps only the LAST module that changed it (`hooks[k] = file` overwrites). chainHook (world.ts:1062-1066) runs hooks in install order, so the chained hook ORDER is not recorded. For example, production playerKilled is recorded as only 'quests', and capture's as only 'killAugments'. That order decides when on-hit, kill and camp-clear reactions run. So legacy_schedule.json cannot verify the hook-chain order a Rust static schedule must reproduce. It should record the ordered list of installing modules per hook (and flag hooks assigned without chainHook).

state_hash covers the queued inputs only as counts and presence bits (actions.len, mv.is_some, aim.is_some). It ignores the queued move target, aim angle, action angles and times, move_before/aim_before and dropped. Two sims that differ only in what was submitted between steps hash the same, so a checkpoint taken between submit and step (C-DET: 'a checkpoint is the serialised Sim') could restore wrong queued inputs with an equal hash. Today this is mostly masked because recorders hash right after step, when the queues are empty.

keep: The damage ledger as one simultaneous pass per tick (ledger.ts, sim.rs apply_ledger): every hit is recorded first. Outgoing multipliers are fixed from pass-start state, each victim's hits are mitigated, capped and applied together, and kill spoils are paid only after every victim took damage (payLater / Rust Payout). This makes outcomes independent of processing order. Generalize Payout into a typed deferred-effect enum, not closures.

The secret per-tick action order (mulberry32 Fisher-Yates keyed by order_salt ^ tick*0x9e3779b1) for fair same-tick races, and rank-ordered hit application for exact kill-credit ties (players by rank, others after, stable sort).

Lag-compensated melee, 'what I saw is what I hit': the attacker and targets are sampled at the clamped rewind time, present walls block, and the history is bounded to MAX_REWIND_MS + TICK_MS (verified bounded in both movement.ts recordHistory and sim.rs:1730-1740, so it is not unbounded).
All move multipliers are read before anyone moves, history is recorded after everyone has moved, and the multiplier floor is MOVE_MULT_FLOOR (a 0 root stays 0).
Deaths during a tick are settled together at settle(): simultaneous deaths are decided by the hp fraction at tick start, and leaves between steps count toward the next tick.
Mobs and bots act only by pushing inputs into their own InputQueue, applied by the same handlers (legacy mobAI contract = C-INPUT); the AI is a system after damage, so a mob reacts one tick late.
InputQueue semantics: the latest move and the latest aim win at their arrival position among the actions, at most 6 actions per tick, and a drop drains the queue and releases the trigger.
Separate RNG streams per purpose (orderSalt, rewardRandom, questRandom), never derived from the public map seed. Rewards are never drawn from a stream whose outcomes clients can stage.

Kill-credit rules: the largest rival hit takes the kill; a recent rival within KILL_CREDIT_SECONDS gets credit otherwise; MIA credit is judged at drop time; a resolved or departed source is credited by name only, with no GV.
Bots never close a lobby and never pay or bank GV; the win bonus is gated by human starters and human opponents damaged.
NaN-safe guards of the form !(x > 0.0), and legacy f64 evaluation order with libm transcendentals (C-NUM).
Events emitted between ticks travel with the next step. Events are typed (Rust's Event enum already designs out legacy's ad-hoc { type, fx } objects), with an important/droppable split.
Fixed 20 Hz virtual sim time, with the pacer dropping a backlog beyond 3 owed steps (time drop never changes an outcome).
f64 millisecond durations with fractional ready_at/lands_at (attack phase carry). Do not quantize to integer ticks (see LC5).

proposals.title: densitybench: an in-process, deterministic-capable host-density benchmark on the real Room/Outbox/Pacer loop
proposals.problem: Capacity is 'not established' (docs/MIGRATION.md:124-125; ADR 0004 item 4 says density is 'decided by measurement'), and nothing can measure it. wirebench (crates/rh-server/src/bin/wirebench.rs:56-106) drives rh_headless::Env, not Room: it skips the pacer, inbound RoomCmd handling, Outbox, writer drain and tokio scheduling. RoomStats only appears when a room closes (room.rs:624-629). The measured cost of a match also varies 4.4x with client behaviour (5.25M Ir per match-second on the practice arena vs 45.9M on seed-1 with far-move orders, find_path at 96%), so one number is meaningless without client profiles. run_room's unbiased tokio::select! (room.rs:661) makes paused-clock runs vary ±1.4% in Ir, too noisy for a gate.
proposals.change: Add crates/rh-server/src/bin/densitybench.rs, generalising the prototype at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RougeHalla/a10579c9-d749-521d-8f53-e9adbb8ce754/scratchpad/audit/server-density/loadbench/src/main.rs. It runs N rooms through the production run_room. Each room gets H scripted clients that send RoomCmd::Input through the room's bounded mpsc like conn.rs, at a configurable rate. Client profiles: idle; legacy-like (click-move to nearby points every 0.5-2 s, attack when an enemy is in the decoded snapshot); worst case (far moves at the full 15/s order budget). Every Outbox is drained by a writer-like task that counts frames and bytes, and an optional --sockets mode uses in-process tokio-tungstenite clients over loopback so the syscall path is covered too. Fill bots top rooms up to 8. Closed rooms are replaced, which keeps the load steady. Modes: --paused (current_thread, start_paused) reports deterministic Ir per match-second under callgrind and allocations per human-tick under dhat; real-time --workers W reports CPU per match-second (getrusage), wake lateness p50/p99/max from a histogram (the SD6 metric, so the production loop needs no fork), dropped steps, ticks achieved vs owed, and VmRSS per room at N = 50/100/200 plus a --ramp mode. Add `biased;` to run_room's select! (deadline branch first) so paused runs are reproducible (measured ±0.002%) and an input flood cannot postpone a due step. Today the choice is random, so this only narrows already-allowed orderings.

proof.metric: (a) Ir per match-second and allocations per human-tick in paused mode; (b) CPU per match-second, p99 wake lateness, dropped steps and RSS per room at N = 50/100/200 in real time
proof.method: Run callgrind 3 times on the paused mode and compare spreads; run real-time mode on an idle host and check it against the paused-mode extrapolation and against the real-socket figure (rh-server + 64 Node clients: 76-81 ms CPU/s for 8 matches).
proof.expected: Paused-mode Ir reproducible within ±0.01% (prototype: 500,976,241 / 500,972,397 / 500,982,577), so a ±1% CI gate is possible. Baselines to reproduce: practice 5.25M Ir per match-second, 11.1 blocks per human-tick in publish; real-time 2 workers N=200 practice 3.24 ms per match-second with p99 lateness 6.9 ms; seed-1 spam overloads 2 workers at N=200 (57,143/60,000 ticks). It turns 'Capacity: not established' into a number per vCPU and per client profile.

proposals.parity_notes: No sim code changes. `biased;` changes only which of two simultaneously ready branches runs first, which is already nondeterministic today. Replays record the order actually applied, so equivalence.rs stays valid.
proposals.contract_impact: None on the wire. C-TICK: the room loop prefers a due step over queued commands when both are ready (document in CONTRACTS C-TICK as clarified, not changed).
proposals.value_for_future: Every mechanic packet (mobs ~204 per match, projectiles, statuses, vision memory) can be gated on Ir per match-second and allocations per human-tick in CI, and host density for ADR 0004 / P-LOAD-2 / P-HOST-4 can be set from measured numbers. Mobs then just raise the per-room cost the same harness reports; a synthetic --extra-actors flag can preview that scaling now.

proposals.title: Set TCP_NODELAY on the production listeners (plain and rustls) and serve tests through the same code path
proposals.problem: main.rs:272-281 serves through axum_server::bind / bind_rustls with the DefaultAcceptor, which never sets TCP_NODELAY (strace: only SO_REUSEADDR on the listener). Every tick the room pushes up to three separate WebSocket messages per client (Events, Fx, Snapshot: room.rs:569/580/584), and the writer sends each with its own flush (conn.rs:124). With Nagle on, the 2nd and 3rd small segments wait for the ACK of the 1st, and clients delay ACKs (Linux up to 40 ms, Windows up to 200 ms). On loopback the snapshot inter-arrival p99 was 77-80 ms with Nagle vs 53-55 ms with TCP_NODELAY (10 Hz ping). The tests miss it because live.rs and equivalence.rs use axum::serve, which does set nodelay (axum serve/mod.rs:519-521).
proposals.change: Build the listener with axum_server::accept::NoDelayAcceptor: `axum_server::bind(addr).acceptor(NoDelayAcceptor::new())`, and for TLS `RustlsAcceptor::new(cfg).acceptor(NoDelayAcceptor::new())` with `axum_server::bind(addr).acceptor(...)`. Move the serve setup from main.rs into a lib function `serve(bind, tls, router, handle)` so a test can start the production stack.

proof.metric: setsockopt(TCP_NODELAY) on every accepted socket; snapshot inter-arrival p99 and Pong RTT p99 over a delayed link
proof.method: strace -f -e trace=setsockopt on rh-server while a client connects; a unit test that runs the acceptor on a loopback TcpStream and asserts stream.nodelay()==true; optionally `tc qdisc netem delay 30ms` in a network namespace with load.mjs before/after.
proof.expected: TCP_NODELAY present on 100% of accepted sockets (0% today). Snapshot gap p99 drops toward the 50 ms tick plus jitter: 77-80 ms became 53-55 ms on loopback already, and the gap grows with real RTT and client delayed-ACK.

proposals.parity_notes: Transport only.
proposals.contract_impact: None (no wire change).
proposals.value_for_future: Removes a latency tail that would otherwise be blamed on the sim or the network in the staging experiment (STAGING_EXPERIMENT.md) and in P-NET-1 prediction tuning.
proposals.legacy_carryover: The legacy Colyseus/uWS stack set nodelay implicitly; the port lost it when it switched from axum::serve (tests) to axum_server (production).

proposals.title: Per-tick batched egress: one Outbox push and one notify per client per tick, one flush per writer wake, no per-frame timers
proposals.problem: Sockets and connections are ~80% of server CPU on the slice: the real server used 76-81 ms CPU/s for 64 humans / 8 rooms (user 36-40, sys 39-40), while the same rooms in-process used ~15.6 ms/s. Each frame costs one syscall (strace: 2,796 sendto in 80 client-seconds = one per WS message). Each also costs one Outbox lock and one Notify (outbox.rs:280-322, called three times per human per tick at room.rs:569/580/584), so the writer task wakes up to three times per tick, often on another worker (2,589 futex + 627 eventfd writes per 80 client-seconds). The writer awaits `timeout(SEND_TIMEOUT, tx.send(..))` per frame, i.e. a timer registration plus a full flush per frame (conn.rs:122-130). The reader creates a fresh `timeout(idle, rx.next())` per inbound frame (conn.rs:160), up to 40+ timer registrations per client-second. The room loop rebuilds its sleep_until on every received command (room.rs:660-667).
proposals.change: (1) Outbox::push_tick(important: Option<Vec<u8>>, fx: Option<Vec<u8>>, snapshot: Vec<u8>) takes the lock once and notifies once, with the same caps and semantics as today. (2) Writer: on wake, pop everything currently queued in today's priority order (important, then Close, then fx, then the latest snapshot) via a new Outbox::drain_into(&mut Vec<Next>), `feed` each frame into the sink, then flush once, all under one `timeout(SEND_TIMEOUT, ...)`. Frames stay separate WebSocket messages; tungstenite buffers them in out_buffer, below write_buffer_size. (3) Reader liveness: keep a last-seen Instant updated per frame and one pinned Sleep reset at most once per second, or check idleness on a 1 s interval, instead of a new Timeout per frame. (4) run_room: pin one Sleep and reset it only after a wake changes the deadline. Optional later step, which needs a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump: a single TickBundle message per tick.

proof.metric: sendto and futex syscalls per client-second; server CPU (utime+stime) per human-second; writer wakes per tick; frame order
proof.method: strace -f -c and /proc/<pid>/stat sampling with node load.mjs (64 clients, 1 Hz and 10 Hz ping) before/after; a densitybench counter of Outbox notifies and writer polls per human-tick; unit tests that the drained batch order equals the order today's repeated next() calls produce (important before Close before fx before snapshot; Close after queued important frames); the existing live.rs tests (rate limit, flooding client, stalled client, resume, liveness) unchanged.
proof.expected: sendto per client-second drops from 25.1 (1 Hz ping) / 34.9 (10 Hz ping) to ≤ ~21 (one per tick plus pongs): -16% to -40%, more in fights and with mobs, where legacy sends 11-15 KB/s per client in more frames. Notifies per human-tick drop from up to 3 to 1. Expect ≥15% less server CPU per human-second (baseline ~1.0 ms ws, ~1.2 ms wss). The extra Timeout per inbound frame goes away entirely.

proposals.parity_notes: No sim change. Frames and their order on the wire are byte-identical. Only syscall grouping changes.
proposals.contract_impact: None (C-NET-5 slow-client semantics kept: important never dropped, snapshot latest-wins, fx bounded, TooSlow at IMPORTANT_CAP).
proposals.value_for_future: Egress cost then scales with ticks, not frames. That matters once mobs, projectiles and status fx multiply per-tick events and fx frames, and with TLS, where every flush is a record. It is the largest per-player CPU lever on the slice.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy Colyseus batched patches per tick inside one message. The port's one-flush-per-message writer is a regression relative to that, not a carryover.

proposals.title: Shrink the per-connection WebSocket read buffer from 128 KiB to 4 KiB
proposals.problem: lib.rs:42-47 configures max_message_size/max_frame_size (1,024 B) but leaves read_buffer_size at tungstenite's 128 KiB default (tungstenite protocol/mod.rs:98). FrameCodec::new then allocates BytesMut::with_capacity(131,072) per connection (frame/mod.rs:125). dhat on rh-server with 64 clients: 8,388,608 B of a 9,139,875 B peak heap (92%) is this buffer. VmRSS grows by 166 KB per human (1.33 MB per 8-human match), versus ~0.62 MB per room in-process.
proposals.change: `upgrade.read_buffer_size(4 * 1024)` (and consider `.write_buffer_size(16 * 1024)`, `.max_write_buffer_size(64 * 1024)` so a stalled peer cannot grow out_buffer without bound beyond SEND_TIMEOUT) in lib.rs ws().

proof.metric: dhat t-gmax bytes and VmRSS per connected human
proof.method: Same dhat and VmRSS runs as the baseline (rh-server + node load.mjs 64/128 clients) before/after.
proof.expected: Peak heap for 64 connections drops from 9.14 MB to ≈1.0 MB (-131,072 + 4,096 B per connection). RSS per human drops from 166 KB to ≈80-90 KB. At 1,600 players: ≈200 MB less allocated, ≈130 MB less resident.

proposals.parity_notes: Transport buffer only. Client frames are already capped at 1,024 B before decode.
proposals.contract_impact: None.
proposals.value_for_future: Per-connection memory then no longer dominates per-match memory, which keeps memory-light instance types and more processes per host open for ADR 0004 packing.
proposals.legacy_carryover: n/a (library default).

proposals.title: Zero-regrowth publish: encode into presized buffers, observe into reused scratch, encode snapshots straight from the Observation, swap event buffers
proposals.problem: Publish allocates ~11.1 blocks per human-tick (dhat, loadbench practice): ServerMsg::encode starts from Writer::default() and regrows (rh-protocol lib.rs:417-418; 570,776 blocks at lib.rs:455 alone, ~6 per snapshot). observe allocates visible/events Vecs per call through a size-hint-less filter().collect() (observe.rs:122-145). wire::snapshot builds an intermediate Vec<WireActor> (wire.rs:421-435) only to encode it. room.rs:523-524 deep-clones every step's events (including RunResult Strings) into last_events and copies them again into all_events. Vec regrowth is 22.6% of wirebench Ir (finish_grow 29.6M of 131.2M), and encode's raw_vec growth is 201M of 322M encode Ir in the density run.
proposals.change: (1) rh-protocol: `ServerMsg::encode_into(&self, out: &mut Vec<u8>)` plus an exact `encoded_len()`; encode() delegates. (2) rh-server wire: `encode_snapshot(&Observation, ack, &mut Vec<u8>)` writes actors straight from ActorView with no Vec<WireActor>; same for Events/Fx. (3) rh-sim: `observe_into(&Sim, viewer, events, &mut Observation)` reusing the caller's Vec capacity (pure, same content); the room keeps one scratch Observation. (4) Room: keep two event Vecs and std::mem::swap instead of clone+extend; publish from last_events when steps == 1. Each outbound frame becomes exactly one allocation of exact size, owned by the Outbox until written. A Bytes freelist can follow if dhat still shows churn.

proof.metric: allocation blocks per human-tick (dhat); Ir per human-tick of observe+encode (callgrind); byte equality of every frame
proof.method: dhat and callgrind on densitybench --paused (practice 10x8, 60 s) and on wirebench before/after; a test that runs wirebench's loop with old and new encoders and asserts byte-identical frames for every player-tick; protocol/fixtures/v1.json unchanged and the C# mirror passing untouched.
proof.expected: Publish allocations drop from 11.1 to ≤3 blocks per human-tick (≥70% fewer; total process blocks -50%). encode Ir -50% or more (the 201M raw_vec growth goes away). wirebench total Ir -15 to -20%. No change in bytes per player per second.

proposals.parity_notes: No sim behaviour change. observe_into must produce an Observation equal to observe (assert equality over a recorded run). Frames are byte-identical.
proposals.contract_impact: API additions only (rh-protocol encode_into, rh-sim observe_into). No wire change, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. C-OBS unchanged.
proposals.value_for_future: Per-human publish cost becomes allocation-free, which matters when ~204 mobs multiply visible actors and events (legacy 11-15 KB/s per client). The policy seam (drive_seats observes every bot every tick) can reuse the same scratch.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy re-serialised Colyseus schemas per client. Building fresh Vecs per frame is that pattern carried into Rust.

proposals.title: Bounded, live telemetry: fixed histograms instead of step_us Vec, real slow-client counters, process-level metrics on /control/health
proposals.problem: step_us is a Vec<u32> that grows to 72,000 entries per room (room.rs:151, 208, 520-522). Its capacity doubles to 131,072, so it holds 524,288 B per room after a match-hour (dhat: 5.24 MB for 10 rooms) and is cloned and sorted at close (room.rs:633-642). Late wakes, dropped steps and step times are only reported once a room CLOSES (room.rs:624-629 → director.rs:464-467, the last 64 rooms). The live tick-deadline-miss guardrail ADR 0004 item 5 relies on does not exist. RoomStats.fx_dropped and snapshots_skipped are hard-coded 0 (room.rs:651-652), although each Outbox counts them (outbox.rs:269-270, 303, 318). bytes_queued only ever increases (outbox.rs:288, 305). Recording a replay costs +43.9% Ir per match, because Sim::state_hash runs every step (replay.rs:100-109; 17.4k Ir per step vs 9.6k for step itself).
proposals.change: (1) A fixed log-linear histogram type (e.g. 4 sub-buckets per power of two from 1 µs to ~2 s, ~84 u32 buckets ≈ 340 B) for step µs, publish µs and wake lateness µs, with exact max and count. RoomStats p50/p99 come from it (documented ≤ ~19% relative bucket error). (2) One process-wide Arc<Metrics> of relaxed atomics updated once per wake (busy ns, lateness bucket, steps, dropped steps, TooSlow/RateLimited closes, fx_dropped/snapshots_skipped summed from Outboxes at close), exposed on /control/health and /info as current window values. (3) Wire the Outbox counters into RoomStats and remove or rename bytes_queued. (4) Keep replay recording off in production; if ops ever wants live recording, hash every 20th step plus the final step (a replay-format decision for C-DET, not part of this packet).

proof.metric: per-room heap at 72,000 steps; quantile error; availability of live lateness
proof.method: dhat on densitybench --paused --idle --secs 3700 (baseline 524,288 B per room for step_us); a unit test comparing histogram p50/p99 with the exact sort over the recorded samples; densitybench reads /control/health-equivalent metrics mid-run and checks them against its own measured lateness.
proof.expected: step_us memory goes from 524,288 B to ≤512 B per room (-99.9%; -105 MB at 200 rooms after an hour), and the O(n log n) close-time sort disappears. Live p99 lateness and busy fraction become available every second instead of after room close. fx_dropped and snapshots_skipped become non-zero under a stalled client (live.rs a_stalled_client_does_not_stall_the_match).

proposals.parity_notes: Telemetry only.
proposals.contract_impact: /info `closedRooms` quantiles become bucketed approximations (documented). New fields on /control/health for the hosting bridge (P-HOST-1 consumes them).
proposals.value_for_future: It is the input for autoscaling guardrails (P-HOST-4), P-OPS-1 tick-deadline misses and SD7 admission. Memory stays flat however long matches run.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy tickPacer.ts tickStats were also per-room arrays reported after the fact. The port copied that shape.

proposals.title: Capacity-aware admission and placement instead of a static --max-rooms count; fullest-lobby-first
proposals.problem: The only capacity gate is a static room count: max_rooms defaults to 16 (director.rs:39, main.rs:162), checked at director.rs:225. The measured cost of a match varies 4.4x with map and client behaviour: practice 3.0-3.3 ms per match-second, seed-1 far-move spam 14.4 ms. A static count either under-packs a host (16 rooms ≈ 5% of a vCPU on the practice workload) or overloads it. Overload degrades EVERY room together (1 worker, seed-1, N=100: p50 lateness 20.9 ms, p99 170.6 ms; N=200 delivered only 55,728 of 80,000 ticks), because the per-room tasks share the workers fairly. Lobby choice iterates a HashMap (director.rs:217-221), so with several open lobbies, players are split arbitrarily rather than filling one. The hosting bridge has no 'available sessions' figure to feed GameLift target tracking (ADR 0004 item 5).
proposals.change: Director admission opens a NEW room only if the live SD6 window shows busy fraction < target (e.g. 0.6 x worker threads) AND p99 wake lateness over the last 10 s < 10 ms AND there is no dropped step; otherwise MatchFull 'no capacity' (same code as today). --max-rooms stays as a hard ceiling. Joining existing lobbies is always allowed. /control/health reports availableRooms = floor((target - busy) / EWMA per-room cost). Lobby pick: the open lobby with the most humans (ties by oldest), deterministically.

proof.metric: rooms admitted, p99 wake lateness and dropped steps under a ramp; mean humans per started match
proof.method: densitybench --ramp (one new room every 0.5 s) on the practice and seed-1-spam profiles, with static --max-rooms vs budget admission; a director unit test with a scripted arrival/leave sequence comparing HashMap-order picks with fullest-first.
proof.expected: Budget admission holds p99 lateness < 10 ms with 0 dropped steps on both profiles, while admitting about 4x more rooms on the practice profile than on seed-1 spam (≈300 vs ≈70 matches per vCPU at 100% in-process, ≈50 per vCPU with sockets at a 60% target). The static count cannot satisfy both profiles. Fullest-first gives more humans per started match (fewer bot fills, fewer rooms) whenever two lobbies are open.

proposals.parity_notes: Placement and admission policy only. A match's simulation is untouched.
proposals.contract_impact: C-NET admission: the 'no capacity' refusal is driven by measured load as well as the count. New /control/health fields for P-HOST-1/P-HOST-4.
proposals.value_for_future: When mobs land, the per-room cost rises and host density adjusts with no re-tuning of --max-rooms. The process can report the capacity signal GameLift queues and autoscaling need.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy used a fixed Colyseus room cap per process. The port kept the static cap.

proposals.title: Share immutable per-map data across rooms and lend pathfinder scratch per worker instead of per room
proposals.problem: Every room owns a deep copy of the arena: director.rs:232 clones it and Room::new moves it into Sim (room.rs:194), 128,464 B per room on seed-1 (tiles + 102 KB component ids). It also keeps another tiles copy for the Welcome (room.rs:193, 25,600 B) and re-encodes the RLE map on every join and resume (room.rs:235-248). Each Sim owns a Pathfinder sized to the map (sim.rs:414; pathfind.rs:19-25, 47-58): 431 KB per room once any path is searched (dhat: 4.31 MB of 6.69 MB peak for 10 rooms, 65%). Each search memsets ~230 KB (g.fill + closed.fill; memset is 3.6% of seed-1 Ir).
proposals.change: (1) Sim holds `Arc<Arena>` (immutable after load). Rooms share it; the Recorder keeps the Arc. (2) The director pre-encodes the Welcome map blob once per arena (Arc<[u8]>) and splices it into Welcome. (3) The Pathfinder becomes caller-lent scratch: `Sim::step_with(&mut StepScratch)`, with Sim::step() keeping today's signature by using an owned scratch for headless and parity. The server keeps one scratch per worker thread (thread_local in rh-server, not in rh-sim) and lends it to whichever room is stepping. rh-sim stays pure, because the scratch is passed in. (4) Optional, coordinated with the sim lens: generation-stamped g/closed arrays remove the per-search memset.

proof.metric: per-room heap at t-gmax and RSS per room on seed-1 with moving humans; parity
proof.method: dhat on densitybench --paused seed-1 10x8 120 s before/after (baseline ~668 KB per room); VmRSS per room in real-time mode at N=200; cargo run -p rh-parity --bin parity-report (13 scenarios + 300 findPath queries must MATCH); the equivalence.rs replay test.
proof.expected: Per-room heap drops from ~668 KB to ≤ ~80 KB (-88%; -117 MB at 200 rooms) and stays flat as rooms are added (scratch scales with worker threads, not rooms). Each join stops re-encoding the RLE map. Parity: identical.

proposals.parity_notes: A* results depend only on the inputs if the scratch reset is complete (g and closed are filled per search; parent is only read for nodes written in the same search). Verify with the 300 findPath parity queries and the full parity report.
proposals.contract_impact: rh-sim API: Sim::arena becomes Arc<Arena>; a new step_with(&mut scratch). Replay format unchanged (Arena serialises the same).
proposals.value_for_future: P-MAP-1 adds terrain, hazard, bush and camp layers, and P-MOBS-1 adds mob pathing, so per-map data and pathfinding scratch grow. Sharing them keeps per-match memory proportional to dynamic state only.
proposals.legacy_carryover: Legacy built a world per room including its own map layers. The port copied that per-room ownership.

bugs.description: `had_human` is declared (room.rs:162) and initialised false (room.rs:219) but never set to true, so the close-when-empty check `self.had_human || now - opened_at >= UNCLAIMED_TIMEOUT` (room.rs:491) only fires 30 s after the room opened. Measured with the real Room/run_room on a paused clock ($S/loadbench/src/bin/leavetest.rs): a human who joins and leaves at 1.00 s leaves a room that starts a bots-only run at 2.05 s, ends at 25.85 s and closes at 30.85 s after 617 steps. A leave at 5.00 s still runs 599 steps before the 30.00 s close. Meanwhile the empty lobby remains joinable and holds a max_rooms slot. Fix: set `self.had_human = true` in join().

The production listeners (axum_server::bind / bind_rustls, main.rs:272-281) use axum_server's DefaultAcceptor and never set TCP_NODELAY (strace: only SO_REUSEADDR). Each tick sends up to three small WebSocket messages per client, each flushed separately (room.rs:569/580/584, conn.rs:124), so Nagle holds the later ones until the first is ACKed, which a client's delayed ACK can stretch by 40-200 ms. Loopback A/B on the same binary with an LD_PRELOAD shim: snapshot inter-arrival p99 77-80 ms vs 53-55 ms. The tests use axum::serve, which sets nodelay, so they cannot catch this.

RoomStats.fx_dropped and snapshots_skipped are hard-coded to 0 (room.rs:651-652), although each Outbox counts them (outbox.rs:269-270, 303, 318). /info `closedRooms` therefore always reports no slow-client shedding. Outbox.bytes_queued (outbox.rs:271) only ever increases and is never read, so it counts bytes ever queued, not a queue depth.

The RoomReport::Phase handler overwrites RoomEntry.humans with the room's seated count (director.rs:485-494). That count excludes admissions the director has reserved (director.rs:262-264) but not yet seated, because they are still acquiring the durable lease. The lobby can then be offered past MAX_PLAYERS. The extra join is refused MatchFull, after which the director marks a still-open lobby as Active (director.rs:317-327), so in a race the player is placed in another room or refused. Count reservations separately from seated humans.

keep: One tokio task plus one bounded inbound mpsc per room, with commands applied in arrival order between steps (room.rs:657-671). I evaluated sharded room schedulers and do not recommend building them now: tokio task polls, timers and Notify together are ~3% of in-process Ir (cg.loadpr: Sleep::poll 37.6M, Notify ~60M, Outbox ~30M of 3.15G), while sim, observe and encode take ~90%. At overload the remedy is admission control (SD7), not a different scheduler. Revisit only if densitybench shows scheduler-induced lateness at the target density.

The Director's std::sync::Mutex: never held across an await, taken only on admission, resume, report and info paths, never on the tick path. There is no contention at 1,600 players (joins are rare events).
Off-tick durable result writes with capped backoff, idempotency and fencing, plus wait_for_writes on exit (director.rs:378-441, main.rs:232-239).

The pacer's fixed grid on virtual sim time with MAX_CATCHUP=3 and backlog dropping (pacer.rs). Wake lateness p50 of ~1.3 ms is tokio's 1 ms timer granularity, which is harmless because sim time is virtual.

Outbox slow-client isolation semantics (outbox.rs: important never dropped with TooSlow at 256, latest-wins snapshot, bounded fx) and conn.rs try_send→TooSlow back-pressure. SD3 keeps these exactly and changes only their batching.
Per-viewer observe → wire filtering (C-OBS) in Room::publish. SD5 changes how it is built, not what is sent.
Replay recording off by default in production (director.rs:42). It costs +43.9% Ir per match on the slice.

architect.summary:
Lead-architect plan for the core optimization sweep. Checked against HEAD 79dfba3. The task text says 7d94332, but three commits have landed since: perfproof x2 and legacy_schedule.json.

Claims I re-verified myself:
- The parity gate is red at HEAD. `cargo test -p rh-parity` fails every_slice_fixture_matches_legacy because fixture_paths loads legacy_schedule.json as a scenario.
- crowded_8 Sim::step costs 40,064,679 Ir, or 11,117 Ir/step (callgrind --toggle-collect='*Sim>::step'). About a quarter of that is in malloc/free.
- legacy_schedule.json records only the last module per hook (schedule.ts `hooks[k] = file`).
- In rh-server: had_human is never set; neither production listener (main.rs:184-189) sets TCP_NODELAY; read_buffer_size is left at tungstenite's default; run_room uses an unbiased select; the director overwrites its reservation count; fx_dropped is hard-coded to 0.
- run_replay has no format check. js_round is (x+0.5).floor(), which is not JavaScript Math.round. is_important is never called. The encoder does not check MAX_ACTORS.

The six audits agree on the main problems:
1. sim.rs is a 1,868-line monolith. 8 of 13 ready packets serialize on it.
2. The tick schedule exists only as comments.
3. Each step makes about 15-19 heap allocations, roughly 26-35% of step Ir.
4. state_hash is a hand-written list with 66 unhashed leaves, and byte-wise FNV makes it cost 17.1k Ir/tick, 2.25x the step it fingerprints.
5. content_hash misses about 16-19 rule numbers.
6. The publish path builds three copies and regrows its buffers (7.4 blocks per viewer-tick).
7. Observations are built for bots that are not due to decide (63% wasted).
8. Server egress makes one syscall and one notify per frame, with no NODELAY and a 128 KiB read buffer per connection.

The plan has 10 packages in 5 parallel groups:
- G1: proof gate and harness repair.
- G2 (five parallel packages): sim module split with an executable schedule table; pathfinder and geometry kernel; content registry; server runtime with densitybench; protocol encoder and the C# mirror.
- G3: fighter data model plus an allocation-free tick.
- G4 (two parallel packages): serde-derived state hash with replay v2 and determinism lints; observation and publish path.
- G5: delta snapshot protocol v2, the only wire change.

Gameplay stays bit-identical throughout. That is proven by the parity report (13 scenarios plus 300 paths), by baseline-recorded replays that keep verifying until the hash is deliberately redefined in P8, and by a new hash-independent outcome digest checked in perfproof fingerprints.
architect.target_architecture:
Goal: the same rules in the same order, but structured so that each of the ~40 backlog packets adds a file plus a table row, never edits a monolith, cannot forget hashing, checkpoint or visibility, and adds no per-tick allocation. Everything below keeps C-TICK order, C-INPUT (validate + Sim::submit only), C-OBS, C-RNG and rh-sim purity.

1. rh-sim module layout (sim.rs becomes a facade of at most 300 lines)
- sim.rs: the public facade only, with new, reset_active, add_player, submit, mark_dropped, remove_player, step, step_into, checkpoint/restore and read accessors. Callers keep compiling: Sim::new takes `impl Into<Arc<Arena>>`.
- statics.rs: `MatchStatic { config: SimConfig, arena: Arc<Arena>, secrets: Secrets, digest: u64 }`. It is immutable once the match starts. Rooms share one Arc<Arena> per map. digest = hash(config, arena layer, spawns, secrets), computed once.
- state.rs: `World { tick, server_time, phase, lobby_ends_at, raid_started_at, players: Store<Player>, roster: Roster, rt: ArenaRt, spawn_rng, next_id, joined, winner, pending_events: Vec<Event> }`. This is the only thing that is serialized (checkpoint) and hashed.
- scratch.rs: `#[serde(skip)] TickScratch`, all per-tick working sets. It holds order, rank-by-slot, bounty-at-start-by-slot, standing, mults, bodies, melee, ledger, victims, first-appearance index, amounts, hits, payouts and alive. Buffers are cleared and reused, never taken. A debug assert checks the tick-local buffers are empty at the end of a step.
- schedule.rs: the tick schedule as static data. PHASES mirrors legacy updateActive's 23 phases. The registration lists (AFTER_WEAPONS 3, BEFORE_DAMAGE 3, SYSTEMS 24, MOVE_MODIFIERS 7 folded left to right, MOD_SOURCES 6), ACTIONS and the ordered HOOKS chains each carry a legacy name `module.fn`, a config gate (signatures, walkHints, training...) and `Run::Ported(fn(&mut Cx))` or `Run::Pending("P-XXX-n")`. update_active is a loop over PHASES. A conformance test projects the tables under the production and capture gate sets and compares them with parity/fixtures/legacy_schedule.json. Example: feed.flushAnnouncements is pinned at systems #6, after fireRoam, factions.afterDamage/healOverTime, mobs.resetDummies and buffs.expireBoosts. A packet ports a system by flipping one row.
- systems/{lobby, inputs, weapons, movement, melee, ledger, credit, settle}.rs: each is `pub(crate) fn run(cx: &mut Cx)`. `Cx<'a> { k: &'a MatchStatic, w: &'a mut World, s: &'a mut TickScratch, ev: &'a mut Vec<Event>, pf: &'a mut Pathfinder }`. Disjoint borrows replace the mem::take workarounds, and each signature shows what the system can touch.
- events.rs: the Event enum plus exhaustive `visibility()` (Everyone, IfSeen(id), SelfOnly(id), IfSeenOrSelf, ServerOnly) and `class()` (Important, Fx, ServerOnly), with no wildcard arms. A new variant fails to compile until its C-OBS and C-NET decisions are made.
- results.rs (RunResult, GvBreakdown), hash.rs, checkpoint.rs, fighter.rs, store.rs. ids.rs is reserved: its first user, the legacy nextId shared counter and tieRank, lands with the first packet that allocates nextId entities.
- Unchanged kernels: geometry.rs, map.rs, pathfind.rs, math.rs, rng.rs, input.rs. They are only made cheaper.

2. Entity and data model
- `EntityId(u32)`, with PlayerId as an alias. It is monotonic and never reused.
- `Store<T>`: a Vec kept in id order, which equals join order and legacy Map insertion order. get is a binary search, remove preserves order, iteration is legacy order. Per-tick ranks and bounty snapshots are dense per-slot arrays, so every lookup that used to be an O(n) scan (idx at 23 call sites, rank_of inside a sort comparator, owed_bounty, victims.contains) becomes O(1) or O(log n).
- `Player { core: FighterCore { id, body (x, y, facing, path + cursor, history ring of 9), vitals (hp, max_hp, barrier, immune_until, hp_frac_at_tick_start), weapon (slots, WeaponRt, ready_at, draw_started_at), inputs }, seat (roster slot, bot, budget, dropped_at), credit (kills, bot_kills, bounty, gv_parts, last_hit, damaged, damaged_humans, killed_by slot, announce), status/down/resolved }`.
- FighterCore is what weapons, movement, melee and ledger operate on. P-MOBS-1 adds `mobs: Store<Mob { core: FighterCore, brain }>` and a `FighterRef::Mob` arm, iterating players then mobs exactly as step.ts does.
- `Roster`: append-only per match, mapping slot to {profile, name, bot}, and it survives leaves. Ledger entries, melee requests and payouts become Copy, with `Source::Fighter(EntityId)` and no String. Names are resolved from the roster only when a RunResult is built, including the departed-shooter fallback. killed_by and winner stay Strings on the wire and in persistence.
- Payouts are a typed `enum Payout`, applied after the pass, replacing legacy's payLater closures. Deferred ledger entries are World state.
- InputQueue holds an inline `[ActionCmd; MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TICK]` plus a len, serialized as a sequence, with the same arrival-order semantics.
- Time stays f64 ms with fractional ready_at. Integer ticks would break attack phase carry.

3. Hashing and checkpoint
- `state_hash = mix(k.digest, HashSer(&world))`. HashSer is a serde::Serializer that feeds 64-bit words (f64 bits, widened ints, enum variant index, length-prefixed sequences and strings in 8-byte chunks) into one multiply-xor-rotate per word.
- What is serialized is exactly what is hashed: scratch is serde(skip) and statics are covered by digest. A generic leaf-perturbation test fails whenever a serialized leaf is invisible to the hash.
- clippy disallows HashMap/HashSet, std transcendentals and Instant/SystemTime::now in rh-sim.
- Derived tables (TileMap comps and nav mask) are built during deserialization (serde try_from), so a restored Sim or Replay is never half-built and a malformed map is an Err, not a panic.
- The replay format becomes rh-replay/2, and run_replay checks it.
- content_hash is folded from one registry that every gameplay constant must be declared in (macro plus a source-scanning test), plus the faction and weapon tables, including timing literals and rule flags such as which weapons stagger.

4. Kernels
- Pathfinder: generation-stamped g/closed (O(explored) reset instead of 25,600-cell fills), a per-tile 8-bit step mask, find_path_into with internal scratch, and string-pull end discs memoized per anchor and candidate. The binary heap, before() epsilon comparator and pull-window scan are kept exactly: the comparator is not transitive, so heap shape is semantics. Clone yields fresh scratch.
- ray_blocked is the hit-only DDA for every line-of-sight caller. floor_i64/ceil_i64 replace the software floor on x86_64 baseline. js_round becomes the exact Math.round.

5. Observation and interest
- observe_into(&Sim, viewer, events, &mut Observation) reuses the caller's buffers. Event filtering uses Event::visibility() and a merge over the id-sorted visible set. Content and order are byte-identical to today's observe(), which stays as a wrapper.
- Seats observe only when due. Viewers stay brute-force over candidates (a grid measured no gain at 204x8), with the sight predicate isolated so P-VISION-1 can swap in sightLine and an exact clearance prefilter.

6. Wire
- rh-protocol gets an exact encoded_len, encode_into and a streaming SnapshotWriter, so there is one byte layout and one allocation per frame. The encoder clamps and asserts MAX_ACTORS.
- The server encodes snapshots straight from the Observation. The C# mirror uses value-type actors and a merge-join sample.
- P10 then introduces protocol v2: server_ms dropped; quantized remote actors; per-connection delta against the last snapshot actually written, encoded in the writer task so skipped snapshots are never encoded.

7. Server runtime
- One tokio task per room stays (scheduler overhead measured about 3%). The select prefers a due step (biased) over a pinned Sleep, which makes paused-clock benches reproducible to ±0.002%.
- One Outbox push and one notify per client per tick. The writer drains in today's priority order and flushes once per wake under one timeout. Reader liveness uses a last-seen timestamp with a coarse timer.
- TCP_NODELAY on both production acceptors through one shared serve() that tests also use. A 4 KiB WebSocket read buffer.
- Bounded log-linear histograms replace the step_us Vec. Outbox counters are wired into RoomStats, and live process metrics appear on /control/health.
- Rooms close at the first wake after their last human leaves. Lobby pick is fullest-first and deterministic. Reservations are counted separately from seated humans. The Welcome map blob is encoded once per arena.
- densitybench (in-process, the real Room/Outbox/Pacer) turns capacity into a measured number per client profile.

How this beats a 1:1 port: legacy's order lived in install order plus push/unshift and chainHook, and the Stage-1 port encoded it as comments. Here it is a test-checked table. Legacy's string ids and Map lookups (which the port degraded to linear scans) become dense ids, Copy ledger records and O(1) slot arrays. Legacy's GC churn (new arrays and Maps every tick) becomes a zero-allocation steady state enforced by DHAT gates. State identity (state and content hashes) is complete by construction instead of by review. Event visibility is a compile-time obligation. The egress path batches per tick. None of this changes what any rule computes or the order rules run in.
architect.harness:
Every package is judged A/B by tools/perfproof/perfproof.py, which already exists at 79dfba3. It builds plain --release binaries for a baseline revision and for the candidate in separate target dirs and measures long-minus-short runs, so start-up and fixture loading cancel out. The metrics are callgrind Ir per unit of work and DHAT blocks/bytes per unit of work. The baseline REV is BASE = the merge commit of P1. Cumulative claims are also reported against BASE, and each package reports against the merge-base it branched from. Wall-clock numbers are never used as evidence on the shared container.

Workloads. Existing ones are kept; P1 adds four and P3 and P4 add the rest:
1. sim_crowded_8: parity-bench crowded_8 1 vs 11, per step.
2. sim_duel_chase: parity-bench duel_chase 1 vs 11.
3. sim_fists_duel: parity-bench fists_duel 1 vs 11.
4. wire_seed1_8bots: wirebench --ticks 400 vs 2400 --map parity/maps/seed1.map.json, per step and per viewer-tick.
5. headless_seed1_8bots: rh-headless --matches 1 vs 4 --players 8 --map parity/maps/seed1.map.json --max-ticks 3000, per tick.
6. headless_arena_8bots: rh-headless --matches 2 vs 10 --players 8 --max-ticks 6000.
7. NEW headless_seed1_recorded: workload 5 plus --replay-out. Its hashing share is (7 − 5) per tick.
8. NEW verify_replay: rh-headless --verify-replay on a replay recorded by workload 7 at the same revision, per step.
9. NEW paths_300: parity-bench paths 1 vs 11, the 300 legacy findPath queries, per query (added in P3).
10. NEW density_practice and density_seed1: densitybench --paused --rooms 10 --humans 8 --secs 60 [--map parity/maps/seed1.map.json], per match-second and per human-tick (added in P5). They are deterministic once run_room's select is biased.
11. NEW scalebench N=8/32/128/212: synthetic brawlers past MAX_PLAYERS behind a cfg(feature="bench") constructor, per step and per fighter (added in P7). Plus wirebench --extra-actors 204/1000 for P10.

Behaviour fingerprints, which perfproof compares and which must be identical unless a package declares a change:

packages.rationale: Every search resets g (25,600 f64) and closed (25,600 u8). On seed1 that is 44.8k Ir per search, 37% of find_path in rh-headless, for about 63 expanded nodes. packages.design: Pathfinder: Node{g, parent, stamp} with base += 2 per search (stamp == base: touched; base+1: closed; anything else: g = inf, open). It clears fully only on u32 wrap. packages.title: State identity by construction: serde-derived word hash over World, coverage test, rh-replay/2 with format check, deserialization-complete restore, determinism lints
packages.rationale: state_hash is a 130-line hand list: 66 of 339 serialized leaves are invisible, including Player.name, queued input contents and gv_parts, and path/history are not length-prefixed. Byte-wise FNV costs 17,139 Ir/tick for 8 players, 2.25x the step it fingerprints and 67% of replay verification. Every packet must remember to extend the list. run_replay never checks the format. The determinism rules in ADR 0007 are enforced only by review.
packages.design: hash.rs: `struct HashSer` implements serde::Serializer. It ignores field names, writes enum variant indices, length-prefixes sequences, maps and strings (8-byte chunks), and mixes one u64 per value with h = (h ^ v).wrapping_mul(K).rotate_left(29) plus a splitmix finalizer at the end. state_hash = mix(k.digest, HashSer(&w)). After P2/P7, the serialized World is exactly the checkpoint and scratch is serde(skip), so hash coverage equals checkpoint coverage. tests/hash_coverage.rs runs a crowded_8 replay to tick 40 and a seed1 bot match to tick 300, serializes World to serde_json::Value, perturbs every leaf one at a time (numbers ±1 ulp or +1, bools flipped, strings mutated, sequence lengths changed), deserializes, and asserts the hash changes, with an empty allowlist. A second test covers MatchStatic through the digest. REPLAY_FORMAT becomes rh-replay/2 and run_replay returns ReplayError::Format on mismatch. start_sim, rh-headless main.rs:19 and after_restore stop calling rebuild(), since TileMap try_from (P3) builds derived tables. after_restore stays as a deprecated no-op for API stability. crates/rh-sim/clippy.toml: disallowed-types HashMap/HashSet; disallowed-methods f64::{sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan2, hypot, exp, ln, powf, mul_add} and std::time::{Instant, SystemTime}::now. packages.title: Observation and publish path: observe_into, exhaustive event visibility/class, due-only bot observation, per-step event filtering, direct snapshot encoding
packages.rationale: Each viewer-tick builds an Observation, a ServerMsg with Vec<WireActor> and a Vec<u8> (7.43 blocks per viewer-tick, 4,365 Ir). drive_seats_with builds observations for seats whose cadence then discards them (63.5% wasted, 17.8% of rh-headless Ir). Event filtering in observe and wire.rs uses `_` wildcards, and is_important is dead, so a new Event variant is silently dropped. On a catch-up wake (2-3 steps), every step's events are filtered against the final step's line of sight: a small C-OBS leak, plus dropped deaths. The room deep-clones events each step.

Seat::wants(tick) is public, drive_seats_with skips observe for non-due seats and reuses one Observation per Seat, and Policy::decide_into has a default that wraps decide (additive, no POLICY_CONTRACT_VERSION bump). rh-headless Env and Room use Sim::step_into with swapped event buffers instead of clone + extend. rh-server wire.rs: encode_snapshot/encode_events/encode_fx(&Observation, ack, &mut Vec<u8>) through P6's SnapshotWriter, using Event::class() instead of hand lists. Room::publish keeps one Observation per human, and wirebench calls the same publish function, so the bench measures production code. Catch-up fix: when a wake runs more than one step, each step's events are filtered with that step's visible set (observe_into after each step, only on multi-step wakes); one Snapshot goes out for the final state. crates/rh-policy/clippy.toml carries the same determinism lints, with #[allow] on Seat's wall-clock budget.

packages.title: Protocol v2 snapshots: drop server_ms, quantized remote actors, per-connection delta encoded in the writer task
packages.rationale: server_ms always equals tick*50 (8 of 89.8 mean bytes). Remote actors are resent in full every tick although x/y change on about 18% of actor-ticks. With ~204 mobs (synthetic) a player gets 7.4 KB/s of snapshots, and with the 30 s vision trail at 1000 actors 31 KB/s, above legacy's 11-15 KB/s gate. Snapshots that latest-wins later discards are still encoded on the room task. This is the cheapest moment for the change: no client renders v1 yet (P-UNITY-1 not started), and P-MOBS-1 must change WireActor anyway.
packages.design: PROTOCOL_VERSION 2. A Snapshot carries tag, tick, phase, ack, flags (full or delta), self as a u16 field mask plus changed fields (self keeps f32 x/y for reconciliation), then actor records: LEB128 id, u8 field mask, changed fields only (x/y as u16 at 1/8 u, facing u8, hp_pct, status, weapon, bounty), and a departed-id list. The baseline is the last snapshot this connection's writer actually wrote (WebSocket is reliable and ordered); Welcome and resume reset it with a full frame. The Outbox snapshot slot holds the structured quantized state (latest-wins), and the writer task encodes the delta at dequeue, so skipped snapshots are never encoded and encoding leaves the room task. Clients derive ServerMs = Tick*50. wirebench gains --wire v1|v2 and --extra-actors N.

open_questions: Protocol v2 (P10) is the only wire change. Should it be done now, before P-UNITY-1 builds rendering on the v1 snapshot shape and while no clients are deployed, or folded into the WireActor change P-MOBS-1 has to make anyway? The plan does it now as the last package. Dropping it costs nothing earlier in the plan.

For an in-test zero-allocation assertion, may the coordinator add the `dhat` crate as an rh-sim dev-dependency? That changes Cargo.lock; its testing mode needs no unsafe code. Without it, allocation freedom is enforced only by perfproof DHAT thresholds, because unsafe_code = forbid rules out a hand-written counting allocator.

critic.verdict: The plan points the right way and almost every step keeps gameplay identical: float order, the A* heap and comparator, action-order use and event order are all preserved. It cannot be executed as written. (1) The main parity proof breaks. "A replay recorded at BASE verifies on the candidate until P8" fails as soon as P4 merges, because run_replay rejects any content_hash mismatch before it compares a single state hash (replay.rs:149-155). P4 sits in G2, so P7 (the riskiest package) and P9 lose their bit-identity proof. (2) P1's hook-order capture records one entry per module. Legacy actually builds hooks three ways: chainHook appends (one module can add several links), hand-written wrappers, and plain overwrites that throw the chain away. So the P2 conformance test would check against a fixture that is wrong. (3) Two parallel-group write conflicts are hidden. P2 cannot keep callers compiling while moving the public Sim fields (sim.tick, sim.arena), and fixing that edits P5's room.rs. P5's pre-encoded Welcome blob needs rh-protocol changes, which belong to P6. (4) P2's cfg(test) execution trace never compiles from an rh-parity test. (5) P6's change of WireSelf from class to struct breaks the Unity scripts that already use it, and CI's sync-net check is not in P6's write scope. (6) P5's CPU-time and strace proofs depend on wall-clock timing. P2, P5, P7 and P10 are each too large for one focused session and should be split. After these fixes, proof sequencing and the C-DET/C-OBS wording are sound.

P4 is in G2, so every later package (P7, P9) loses the obligation 'BASE-recorded replay verifies on the candidate until P8'. P7 is the package that most needs it: medium risk, data-model rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Clamping the count and the written actors' makes the encoder pick which actors a client sees. C-OBS says 'Clients and policies receive the same observation' (docs/CONTRACTS.md C-OBS), so a silent clamp makes the client's view diverge from the Observation and hides a visibility decision inside the codec.
issues.fix: Keep the debug_assert and return an encode error (counted and logged) instead of clamping silently. Put the cap rule in observe, decided with P-VISION-1, with a test that observe never exceeds MAX_ACTORS.

issues.problem: The hash-identity claim depends on representation details the plan does not pin down. state_hash feeds path and history element by element (sim.rs:1561-1569). With a cursor, the consumed prefix must be neither hashed nor serialized, or BASE replays diverge and P8's serde hash would cover dead data. The history bound of 8 holds only because of record_history's trim loop (sim.rs:1730-1740: `len > 2 && h[0].t < cutoff`); a fixed 9-ring that is only debug-asserted would silently drop samples in release if a later packet changes MAX_REWIND_MS. rh-headless/Cargo.toml, needed to forward rh-sim/bench to scalebench, is missing from the write scope.
issues.fix: Serialize and hash only the logical content: path[cursor..], and history oldest-first. Compact the path when it is replaced. Check history capacity with a hard assert or a const assert derived from MAX_REWIND_MS/TICK_MS. Add rh-headless/Cargo.toml (feature `bench = ["rh-sim/bench"]`) to the scope.

issues.problem: MatchStatic.digest mixes the secrets into state_hash. That adds no divergence detection: secrets are constant per match, replays already store them, and C-DET compares runtime to runtime. It does make the hash secret-derived, and room.rs:627 already ships final_hash in RoomReport::Closed. If the hash is ever logged or exported (P-OPS-6, /info), it becomes an offline oracle against the 32-bit secrets (C-RNG).
issues.fix: Exclude secrets from the digest (hash config, map layer and spawns only). Document in C-RNG/C-DET that state_hash is server-only.

issues.problem: The serde-derived hash and the JSON-based coverage test assume every leaf round-trips through serde_json. serde_json writes NaN and ±inf as null, so a non-finite f64 in World breaks JSON checkpoints and can be neither perturbed nor restored. The backlog uses -Infinity sentinels (P-COMBAT-3), and today only locals hold them (sim.rs:1351, :1422). Separately, serde attributes such as skip_serializing_if or flatten on World types would make HashSer ambiguous: a missing Option tag, or map-shaped structs.
issues.fix: Add a determinism lint test: walk World with a validating Serializer that fails on non-finite f64 and on skipped or flattened fields (or represent sentinels as Option). Document it in ADR 0007.

issues.problem: P9's proof says 'identical on every viewer-tick', but its catch-up fix intentionally changes frames on multi-step wakes. 'A merge over the id-sorted visible set' does not apply, because events are in emission order, not id order. Due-only observation is exact today only because a seat's obs.events holds only the last step's events and is thrown away on non-due ticks (room.rs:504-523; rh-policy lib.rs:111-114). That event-delivery rule for policies was never decided, and P-BOTS-1 may need events accumulated since the last decision.
issues.fix: Scope byte-identity to single-step wakes and test the catch-up change separately (paused clock, 3 owed steps, attacker leaving sight). Filter with a binary search on the sorted visible list or a per-call slot bitset. Decide and document the C-POLICY rule (drop vs accumulate events between decisions) in P9. If accumulate, skip-observe becomes 'accumulate events, skip actor scan'.
